title: Content Creator in Residence @Health Startup
description:
Wir bauen die Marke, auf die unsere Eltern gewartet haben. Bau sie mit uns! ✨

Die meisten Menschen denken bei Muskeln an Fitnessstudio und Bodybuilding. Wir denken an Lebensqualität. Denn Muskeln sind das Fundament eines aktiven Lebens. Sie halten uns beweglich, unabhängig und leistungsfähig im Alltag.

Fortisana ist unsere Antwort darauf: ein wissenschaftlich fundierter All-in-One-Drink rund um Muskelerhalt und ein aktives Leben. Wir stehen am Anfang – und du kannst mitprägen, wie Menschen uns kennenlernen.

Hinter Fortisana stehen Piran, Leon und Max:

  • Piran hat KoRo mitgegründet und über neun Jahre zu einer der erfolgreichsten Lebensmittelmarken Deutschlands aufgebaut.

  • Leon ist Ernährungsberater und in der Welt der Nahrungsergänzung aufgewachsen. Seine Familie produziert seit über 25 Jahren Nahrungsergänzungsmittel in Deutschland.

  • Max hat bereits mehr als sechs Startups begleitet und zuletzt bei 1KOMMA5° gelernt, wie aus einer Vision ein operativ exzellentes Unternehmen wird.

Was du bei uns machst

  • Du übernimmst unseren Markenauftritt auf Social Media. Von der Strategie über die kreative Idee bis zum fertigen Beitrag entwickelst du Inhalte mit einer klaren Handschrift.

  • Du setzt selbst um. Du entwickelst starke Einstiege, planst Drehs, filmst und schneidest Kurzvideos – von Produktaufnahmen über Interviews bis zu Einblicken hinter die Kulissen.

  • Du lernst aus den Ergebnissen. Du veröffentlichst, hörst der Community zu und nutzt ihre Fragen und die Leistungsdaten deiner Beiträge, um die nächsten Ideen besser zu machen.

Was du mitbringst

  • Du verstehst Social Media. Du kannst Geschichten erzählen und bei Menschen eine Reaktion auslösen. Dein Portfolio zeigt, was du selbst umgesetzt hast.

  • Du hast ein gutes Gespür. Für Ästhetik, Sprache, Timing und die Details, die aus einem ordentlichen Video ein richtig gutes machen.

  • Du denkst mit. Sport, Ernährung und Markenaufbau interessieren dich. Du vermittelst Gesundheitsthemen verständlich und sorgfältig, ohne übertriebene Versprechen.

  • Du packst an. Du bringst eigene Ideen ein und hast Freude daran, sie selbst auf die Straße zu bringen.

  • Du kommunizierst sicher. Ausgezeichnete Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sind Voraussetzung. Du formulierst in beiden Sprachen sicher, präzise und zielgruppengerecht.

  • Du bist vor Ort. Du bist in Berlin oder bereit, für mindestens sechs Monate hierherzukommen.

  • Du arbeitest AI-native und mit Qualitätsanspruch. Du testest eigenständig neue KI-Tools und kreative Ansätze und integrierst sie sinnvoll in deine Workflows. Dabei prüfst du die Ergebnisse kritisch und hältst unseren Qualitätsstandard bei Inhalt, Gestaltung und Genauigkeit hoch.

  • Ein Plus: Erfahrung mit Animation oder Sounddesign.

Was wir dir bieten

  • Verantwortung ab dem ersten Tag. Deine Ideen und deine Arbeit prägen die Marke. Du bekommst Freiraum, Dinge auszuprobieren und eigene Entscheidungen zu treffen.

  • Du lernst, wie ein Startup entsteht. Mit direktem Feedback von Gründern, die wissen, wie man starke Verbrauchermarken aufbaut. Achterbahnfahrt inklusive.

  • Du arbeitest mit uns. Wir sind ein kleines Team. Gute Ideen werden gehört, Einsatz wird wertgeschätzt und du siehst, was deine Arbeit bewegt.

  • Du entwickelst dich weiter. Von Markenstrategie und Zielgruppenverständnis über Storytelling bis zu Produktion, Schnitt und KI.

  • Du wächst mit uns. Unsere Ambition ist groß. Wenn wir abheben, fliegst du mit uns.

Lust, dabei zu sein?

Uns interessiert, wie du denkst und was du richtig gut kannst. Ein perfektes Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Zeig uns lieber deine Arbeit. 🤎

Sag bei jeder Arbeit konkret, was von dir stammt: Idee, Skript, Dreh, Schnitt oder Veröffentlichung – und ob sie im Job, für einen Kunden oder als eigenes Projekt entstanden ist. title: Senior AI Engineer (all genders)
description:
About GeneralMind

GeneralMind builds AI Systems of Action for complex enterprise workflows. We deploy AI employees that automate messy operational handovers across supply chains - processing orders, validating invoices, coordinating suppliers, and handling exceptions directly on top of enterprise systems like SAP, Oracle, JDE, and Dynamics.

Our platform combines AI agents, operational context graphs, and real transaction data to achieve Autopilot-grade automation in real operational environments.

We work closely with leading global companies across manufacturing, retail, and logistics to deploy AI into mission-critical workflows.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer who treats LLMs as production software, not as magic. Someone who can own the agent layer of our platform end to end - from prompt and context design, through tool use and orchestration, to evals, reliability, and continuous improvement in live customer environments.

This role sits at the intersection of two things that are rarely mastered together: shipping LLM-powered systems that actually work in messy enterprise reality, and the discipline of a real engineer - evals, observability, cost, latency, failure modes. Models get smarter every month. What stays scarce is the engineering judgment to make them reliably useful on top of SAP, Oracle, and the mess of real operational data.

You will be a senior individual contributor working directly with the founders. The person in this role won’t be handed a roadmap - they’ll help define it, and build the AI practice around it.

What you will do

AI Ownership

  • Own the agent layer end-to-end: prompt and context design, tool use, orchestration, evals, and long-term technical direction.

  • Be the person who understands why an agent made the decision it made - and who other engineers come to when a model behaves in ways they can’t explain.

  • Set the bar on how we build with LLMs: eval-driven development, context engineering, structured outputs, cost and latency discipline.

  • Make foundational decisions with conviction - which model, which pattern, which guardrail - document the reasoning, and evolve them as the system grows.

LLM Systems in Production

  • Design agents that survive real enterprise environments: ambiguous inputs, flaky upstream systems, exception cases that weren’t in anyone’s spec.

  • Build the eval harness that lets us ship confidently: offline evals, online evals, regression suites, human-in-the-loop review.

  • Think in failure modes: hallucinations, silent drift, prompt injection, tool misuse. Build the detection before you need it.

  • Own cost and latency as first-class product requirements, not afterthoughts.

Agent & Context Engineering

  • Design agent architectures that compose cleanly: tool selection, state, memory, planning, escalation.

  • Build the context layer that makes agents actually useful on top of SAP and Oracle data - retrieval, grounding, schema awareness, auditability.

  • Evolve agents without breaking live customer deployments; manage prompt and model versioning with intention.

  • Know when the right answer is a bigger model, a better prompt, a fine-tune, a tool, or just classical code.

Reliability & Systems Thinking

  • Detect regressions in agent behavior before a customer does; build the evals and observability to catch them early.

  • Own the operational posture of the AI systems you ship: alerting, runbooks, replay, on-call readiness.

  • Identify structural debt in prompts, pipelines, and context before it compounds; refactor with thought.

What we are looking for

  • Experience: 6+ years building production software, with clear ownership of LLM-powered systems in real customer environments - not demos, not notebooks.

  • LLM depth: Non-negotiable. You’ve shipped agents or LLM features that run on live traffic. You have strong opinions about prompting, context, tool use, structured outputs, and what breaks in production.

  • Evals as a first instinct: You don’t ship LLM code without a way to measure it. You’ve built eval pipelines that actually catch regressions, not just vibes.

  • Python depth: You’re fluent in Python and comfortable in production service codebases. You make deliberate calls about async, framework choice, and performance.

  • Reliability instinct: Hallucination containment, idempotency on tool calls, graceful degradation when a model is wrong - part of how you design, not patched in later.

  • End-to-end ownership: You’re comfortable being the person who holds the full agent picture - from prompt to production incident. You identify what’s broken or missing before you’re asked.

  • A real spike: We’re a strong team with broad coverage. What we’re hiring for is someone who brings a 10x improvement in an area we’re currently underinvested in. That might be agent evaluation, context engineering on enterprise data, agentic reliability, deep NLP/LLM internals, or domain-specific grounding. We don’t know exactly what shape it takes - but you should know what yours is, and be able to articulate why it matters.

title: Head of Change.org, Germany - (snr Communications Manager)
description:
Change.org is looking for a (Senior) Communications Manager to lead our team in Germany, as Head of Change.org, Germany. Your job is to make the country notice. You will create big, viral campaigns, online and offline, that put the everyday people who start petitions on Change.org at the centre of the national conversation. The job also involves being the public voice of Change.org in the German media. You will lead a small, high-performing team, open doors through an exceptional network, and use AI to move faster than anyone else in the news cycle.

We'd welcome ambitious Communications Manager level candidates with leadership presence, who are ready to step up into a team leadership role.

Change.org is the world's largest petition platform, used by more than 100 million people every year to take part in civic life and democracy. At a time when dissatisfaction with democracy is at an all-time high, we are investing heavily in AI to build the most powerful tools in the world to give people a voice, while bringing people across the political spectrum together around shared solutions.

What you will achieve

  • Create awareness spikes. Regularly turn petitions from Change.org petition starters into national moments that people talk about, through viral campaigns that combine top-tier media, social media, video, creators and offline actions such as stunts, petition handovers and public events.

  • Put petition starters in the spotlight. Find the strongest stories and the most credible, unexpected voices, and give them the visibility they need to win.

  • Earn trust across the political spectrum. Make sure Change.org campaigns speak to people across the democratic political spectrum, and protect the trust in our brand as the team moves fast with AI. At a Senior Manager level, build balance checks into how the team works.

  • Mobilise your network. Use and grow high-trust relationships with senior editors, producers, journalists, politicians, decision makers, civil society and creators to secure top-tier coverage and move decision makers.

  • Be our voice. Act as Change.org's external spokesperson in Germany on TV, radio, in print and on stage, representing a trusted, open platform for people across the democratic political spectrum, including in sensitive and crisis situations.

  • Lead a high-performing team. Set clear goals, coach and develop people, give direct feedback, and build a culture of speed, ambition and ownership. At a Senior Manager level, set team objectives, coach and develop each person on the team.

  • Lead with AI. Build AI and agentic workflows into how the team spots stories, plans campaigns, pitches media and reports results, so the team works faster and smarter.

What you bring

  • A track record of viral campaigns. You have created campaigns that broke through nationally and drove measurable spikes in public attention, online and offline. You think in moments, images and headlines, and you move from idea to execution in hours, not weeks.

  • Fast paced. You are skilled in fast and excellent execution with rapid pivots and changing contexts.

  • A strong network. You have trusted relationships with German journalists, editors and producers (ideally including key decision makers), and connections in politics and civil society across the whole democratic political spectrum, including conservative circles. You can use your contacts to place stories.

  • Management. You have led and developed a team, or have mentored others and are ready to step into leading one. You set priorities, give direct feedback and bring out the best in people. At a Senior Manager level, you would move resources as the news and priorities shift.

  • Leadership presence. You are confident, credible and calm under pressure. You are an experienced, media-trained spokesperson on live TV and radio and in front of senior stakeholders, and you handle tough interviews, crisis moments and politically sensitive questions with ease.

  • AI First: You use AI tools every day and have built or improved workflows and automations with them. You know where AI adds speed and quality and where human judgement matters most, and you bring your team along.

Target experience

  • 5-8+ years in communications, campaigning, political communications, a newsroom or an agency.

  • 3+ years leading people, at Senior Manager level. We're also open to candidates at Manager level who have experience mentoring others and the ambition to lead a team.

  • A proven track record of national campaigns in Germany that created significant public attention and media coverage.

  • Experience as an organisation's spokesperson in national broadcast and / or print media.

  • Hands-on experience using AI in communications or campaigning work.

  • Native-level German (C2) and professional English.

Interested? Great! Here's what you should know

This role is based in Berlin. It is a full-time hybrid role, and we expect you to be in the Berlin office 2-3 days per week, with flexibility to work remotely for the rest of the week.

Our compensation philosophy is based on pay equity. All of our salaries are determined before we launch a role, based on a predetermined salary scale, the level on that scale and the cost of labour for that location. The annual salary for this role at Senior Manager level is €95,500 in Berlin. We are also open to candidates at the Manager level and the annual salary in Berlin is €83,500.

We recognise that people assess their qualifications differently, and you may not meet every requirement listed. If you believe you could be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply. Change.org is an open platform designed to serve people across the full range of viewpoints. Effectively supporting that mission requires teams with a wide variety of experiences, skills and perspectives, which we consider essential to our work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, age, or any other status protected by law.

We're committed to protecting your data. To learn more, please review our Change.org Job Applicant Privacy Policy.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout our recruitment process. If you need assistance or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know.

Professional-level English proficiency is required for all roles. While we are a global company, we ask that all CVs and application responses be submitted in English.

title: Staff Analytics Engineer
description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

This is a senior individual contributor role in our Data Services & Governance team where you'll act as the thought and technical leader owning the semantic layer and analytics standards for Pleo. This means that you won't own a domain but you'll own what good looks like across all of them by developing, improving , maintaining and evangelising our modelling standards and AI-augmented development practices that every Analytics Engineer work with, regardless of which team they sit in.

The semantic layer you will be designing and maintaining will be the single source of truth that AI agents, BI tools, and analysts query. This is foundational work with company-wide reach which will be ideal for you if you enjoy building things from the ground up. Our semantic layer is still in very early stage. Tooling selection is live, and this role has a strong voice in it. Our BI stack is also in transition so, you would not be inheriting a mature setup and maintaining it. You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it.

For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot.

Who you'll work with

You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. Your primary relationship will be with Analytics Engineers embedded across the Intelligence function who should come to you for architecture guidance, semantic layer decisions, and standards questions. You will also partner with a Staff Data Engineer on data engineering standards and pipeline practices, and with others on self-serve analytics and BI tooling governance. You'll engage with the Data Serving team on entity definitions and with the GenAI Platform team on what AI-ready data looks like at the platform boundary.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the semantic layer: define what a metric definition is, how it's structured, where it lives, and how it's enforced. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational.

  • Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity.

  • Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick.

  • Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it.

  • Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform.

  • Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention.

  • Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream.

  • Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow.

What you bring

  • Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage.

  • Deep BigQuery and SQL expertise, including performance, cost considerations, and the architectural challenges of complex analytical domains.

  • Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust.

  • AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase.

  • A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority.

  • Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime.

  • Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business.

Why this role is a good fit for you

This role is a good fit if:

  • You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy.

  • You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards.

  • You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with.

This role is not a good fit if

  • You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to.

  • You advise others to use AI coding tools but don't use them yourself. AI-native development is part of the mandate, not a differentiating nice-to-have.

  • You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use.

Your first 6 months

By the end of your first six months, you'll have:

  • Mapped the current state of modelling standards and the semantic layer across the function (where definitions are consistent, where they diverge, and what the highest-impact gaps are) to draft a plan the function has bought into.

  • Contributed to the semantic layer tooling decision and begun onboarding the Analytics Engineers who'll build to it by writing documentation, running live sessions, reviewing PRs etc.

  • Established a visible presence in the AE community of practice and become someone whose feedback in code reviews and whose opinions on architecture are listened to because they've been demonstrated, not just stated.

  • Run your own workflow on AI coding tooling to the point where you can say clearly what the function should adopt, what it should not, and why.

The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

  2. Core skills test: A technical test you'll be taking through an external platform to showcase your grasp of analytics engineering fundamentals.

  3. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute conversation-based interview aimed at deep diving into your previous experience and learning more about the team.

  4. Pleo Challenge: A live practical and technical interview designed to assess your problem solving skills as well as your technical expertise.

  5. Final interview: A 45-minutes interview with one of our senior leaders, focusing on assessing behavioural skills and values alignment.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:

  • We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you—not AI—know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background.

  • Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

  • This is a Staff level role at Pleo. This means it's a very senior position where you need to demonstrate experience leading technical initiatives that can have organisation-wide or cross-team impact for a tech business of 500-1000+ people. Prior experience owning a semantic layer is also a non-negotiable. Make sure your application reflects this.

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

Joko is the AI shopping app that helps millions of people save time and money: 7 million users, 10,000 merchants and a team of ~120 people from 18 nationalities, heading to 200+ by the end of 2027.   • Deploy an MDM solution for centralised device management (device fleet, configuration, compliance).

✨ What would make the difference (nice to have)

Atouts

title: Senior contractmanager (domein IT)
description:
Wil jij ervoor zorgen dat belangrijke contracten niet alleen goed zijn afgesloten, maar gedurende de hele looptijd ook daadwerkelijk waarde leveren? En krijg jij energie van leveranciers uitdagen, risico’s beheersen en samen met de business sturen op prestaties en verbetering? Kies dan voor Univé!

Wie zijn wij?

Het mooie van Univé? Dat zijn de mensen, de resultaten, de geschiedenis, de cultuur, het ontstaan en de betrokkenheid. Dat is samenwerken. Een coöperatie zijn zonder winstoogmerk. Dicht bij onze leden staan. En samen bouwen aan een organisatie die betrouwbaar, toekomstbestendig en wendbaar is.

Wij richten ons op het voorkomen van risico’s, het beperken van gevolgen en we verzekeren alleen als het echt nodig is. Coöperatie Univé bestaat uit zeven verschillende Regionale Univé’s, zodat we op landelijk én lokaal niveau altijd dichtbij onze leden zijn. Dat is het mooie van Univé.

Waar kom je te werken?

Je komt te werken binnen de afdeling Inkoop & Facilitaire Zaken, in het team Inkoop & Contractmanagement. Dit team voert binnen Univé de regie op inkoop-, contract- en leveranciersmanagement. Ons doel? Grip op uitgaven en risico’s, professionele en efficiënte processen én optimale ondersteuning van de business.

We zijn volop in ontwikkeling. Inkoop & Contractmanagement groeit verder naar een professionele, businessgerichte en datagedreven regiepartner. Dat betekent dat we niet alleen kijken naar wat er contractueel is afgesproken, maar vooral ook naar de waarde die contracten en leveranciers gedurende de looptijd daadwerkelijk voor Univé realiseren.

Als contractmanager speel jij daarin een belangrijke rol. Je werkt intensief samen met contracteigenaren, management, inkopers, Risk, Compliance en Juridische Zaken. En natuurlijk met onze leveranciers.

Jouw uitdaging

Als contractmanager ben jij verantwoordelijk voor het realiseren en bewaken van contractwaarde gedurende de volledige looptijd van onze contracten.
Je voert regie op het contract- en leveranciersmanagement van de aan jou toegewezen contracten en leveranciers. Daarbij stuur je op naleving van afspraken, kosten, kwaliteit, risico’s, performance, compliance en duurzaamheid.

Je zorgt ervoor dat Univé grip houdt op de ingekochte dienstverlening en dat afspraken niet alleen op papier goed geregeld zijn, maar in de praktijk ook worden nagekomen.

Daarbij ben je een stevige gesprekspartner voor zowel de business als leveranciers. Je organiseert en leidt leveranciersoverleggen, maakt prestaties en risico’s inzichtelijk en zorgt dat acties daadwerkelijk worden opgevolgd. Zie je afwijkingen, kansen of risico’s? Dan wacht je niet af, maar kom je in actie.

Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:

  • regie voeren op complexe, risicovolle en/of strategische contracten;

  • sturen op contractnaleving, kosten, kwaliteit, performance, risico’s, compliance en duurzaamheid;

  • organiseren en leiden van leveranciersoverleggen;

  • bewaken van SLA’s, KPI’s, afspraken en verbetermaatregelen;

  • begeleiden van wijzigingen, indexaties, evaluaties, verlengingen en beëindigingen;

  • signaleren en beheersen van contractuele, leveranciers- en continuïteitsrisico’s;

  • initiëren en begeleiden van verbeterplannen, disputen en escalaties;

  • ondersteunen van contracteigenaren en management bij besluitvorming over contracten en leveranciers;

  • opstellen van analyses en managementrapportages over contractstatus, prestaties, risico’s, acties en besluitpunten;

  • tijdig signaleren wanneer hercontractering of een nieuwe marktbenadering nodig is;

  • bijdragen aan de verdere professionalisering van contract- en leveranciersmanagement binnen Univé.

De inhoudelijke beoordeling van de dienstverlening ligt primair bij de business en contracteigenaar. Jij zorgt ervoor dat deze prestaties periodiek worden beoordeeld en voert regie op de contractuele borging, opvolging en eventuele escalatie. Je kijkt daarbij verder dan één overleg of één contractmoment.

Wie ben jij?

Je bent een contractmanager die regie pakt. Je brengt structuur, houdt overzicht en weet wanneer je moet verbinden, adviseren, onderhandelen of juist escaleren.

Je voelt je comfortabel in een omgeving waarin verschillende belangen samenkomen. Je kunt schakelen tussen de dagelijkse praktijk en tactisch-strategische vraagstukken en bent een stevige gesprekspartner voor contracteigenaren, management en leveranciers.

Je bent analytisch en risicobewust, maar vooral ook gericht op resultaat. Een contract is voor jou geen statisch document: je gebruikt het als instrument om prestaties te verbeteren, risico’s te beheersen en waarde voor Univé te realiseren.

Je bouwt aan professionele leveranciersrelaties waarin transparantie, voorspelbaarheid, continue verbetering en wederzijdse aanspreekbaarheid centraal staan. Je durft leveranciers uit te dagen en weet tegelijkertijd hoe je een constructieve langetermijnrelatie onderhoudt.

Verder breng je mee:

  • HBO/HBO+ werk- en denkniveau, bijvoorbeeld in bedrijfskunde, rechten, economie of een vergelijkbare richting;

  • minimaal 5 jaar relevante ervaring binnen contractmanagement, bij voorkeur domein IT;

  • aantoonbare ervaring met complexe, risicovolle en/of strategische contracten en leveranciers, binnen het domein IT;

  • kennis van contract lifecycle management, leveranciersrelatiemanagement, prestatiesturing en contractgovernance;

  • ervaring met leveranciersoverleggen, prestatiebeoordelingen, contractevaluaties en escalatiemanagement;

  • kennis van risicomanagement, compliance-eisen en interne beheersing;

  • kennis van relevante wet- en regelgeving en uitbestedingskaders;

  • bij voorkeur een aanvullende opleiding op het gebied van contractmanagement, zoals CATS, NEVI 2 of vergelijkbaar.

Daarnaast herkennen we in jou initiatief, regievoering, risicobewustzijn en resultaatgerichtheid. Je bent communicatief sterk, kwaliteitsgericht en analytisch, kunt goed samenwerken en beschikt over overtuigingskracht en onderhandelingsvaardigheden op tactisch-strategisch niveau.

Wat bieden wij?

We vragen veel van je, maar daar geven we je ook graag veel voor terug:

  • een salaris passend bij jouw kennis, opleiding en ervaring op basis van een 38-urige werkweek, inclusief vakantiegeld en een dertiende maand;

  • een collectieve prestatiebeloning;

  • een arbeidsvoorwaardenkeuzesysteem: tijd voor geld of geld voor tijd;

  • 26 vakantiedagen bij een 38-urige werkweek;

  • een studiekostenregeling en volop ruimte om jezelf professioneel verder te ontwikkelen;

  • een goede pensioenvoorziening;

  • hybride werken: thuiswerken is bij ons heel normaal en je hebt de vrijheid om samen met je team je ideale werkplek te bepalen;

  • een reiskostenvergoeding voor woon-werkverkeer en een thuiswerkvergoeding op de dagen dat je vanuit huis werkt;

  • een laptop en telefoon;

  • korting op schade- en zorgverzekeringen.

Maar minstens zo belangrijk: je krijgt bij ons ruimte om impact te maken. Contract- en leveranciersmanagement is binnen Univé volop in ontwikkeling. Je krijgt daarmee de mogelijkheid om niet alleen contracten professioneel te managen, maar ook actief bij te dragen aan hoe we ons vakgebied verder vormgeven.

At Priva Energy, we build software systems that help customers manage and optimize energy in real-world environments, from greenhouses to buildings. You'll join one of our Energy Solutions teams (spanning Building Automation, Horticulture, and Energy Flexibility Trading), landing wherever the need is greatest at the time, and you'll also carry some responsibility for the cloud infrastructure and scalability that benefits teams beyond your own. 

You'll work at the intersection of three things: shipping features end-to-end in Priva Digital Services (touching both backend and, where needed, the front end), integrating optimization and forecasting logic into production services, and strengthening the cloud/DevOps foundation the whole department builds on. You don't need to be equally deep in all three, but you do need to be comfortable moving between them, and you should genuinely enjoy the connective, systems-level work of making things run reliably in production. 

 

Come Shape the Future of Sustainable Energy with Priva 

Priva Energy is working to become the leading global lifecycle partner for high-performing, sustainable buildings, horticultural operations, and energy distribution and management companies. Energy systems are transforming fast: grid congestion, dynamic pricing, decentralized production, and tightening sustainability regulation are reshaping what our customers need from us. Our Digital Twin and optimization technologies exist to meet that shift at scale, delivering measurable results such as lower energy intensity, greater flexibility and reliability, reduced operating costs, and structurally lower emissions. 

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you'll help turn that ambition into production reality: building the services, integrations, and cloud foundation that put our optimization and forecasting capabilities to work for customers every day. 

 

Your work will directly contribute to: 

  • Reducing and optimizing energy costs and emissions across Europe 

  • Enabling customers to participate in future energy flexibility and trading markets 

  • Optimizing multi-energy systems (heat, cold, electricity, storage, HVAC) 

  • Driving the transition toward autonomous, intelligent buildings and greenhouses 

  • Helping customers stay compliant with increasing regulatory pressure (e.g., CSRD) 

 

What You’ll Do 

Priva Digital Services & product engineering 

  • Design and build backend services that process data and execute optimization logic for products across Neo Heat, Neo Light, Neo Building, and Neo Smart 

  • Contribute to user-facing Priva Digital Services features end-to-end, including front-end work where it's the fastest path to shipping value 

  • Build and maintain APIs for internal and external integration 

Optimization & forecasting integration 

  • Implement and integrate optimization and forecasting logic into scalable, production-ready systems. You bring these models into production; you don't develop new optimization theory 

  • Work on data processing pipelines, scheduling logic, and system orchestration 

Cloud infrastructure & DevOps 

  • Own and improve cloud infrastructure (Azure) that supports scalability across Energy Solutions teams 

  • Strengthen CI/CD, monitoring, and deployment practices so systems are reliable, performant, and maintainable in real-world operation 

  • Collaborate with product, domain experts, and other engineers across teams to deliver end-to-end solutions 

  • Contribute to technical design decisions within your domain, and participate in the full software lifecycle: ideation → design → development → testing → deployment → monitoring 

 

What you will NOT do 

  • This is not a research or modelling role. You implement and integrate optimization and forecasting models rather than developing new theory 

  • You are not expected to be a dedicated front-end specialist or a dedicated DevOps specialist. The role spans these areas by design, so depth in every direction isn't the bar 


  • A bachelor's degree in an IT-related field 

  • Around 5 years of experience in a software engineering role, with demonstrated range across at least two of the following: backend/production systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end, or optimization integration. Versatility across these areas matters more here than deep tenure in a single one 

  • You've taken systems into production and kept them running, and can show or talk us through examples (work projects, open source, side projects) 

  • Experience with one or more of the following is a significant advantage: Python, Azure, Docker, Kubernetes/CI-CD tooling, SQL, KQL, Linux, and front-end frameworks (e.g., React/TypeScript) 

  • You are based in the Netherlands and are available to be in the office two to three days per week  

  • Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to work with complex, unfamiliar systems 

  • A passion for creating customer value through high-quality engineering 

  • Curiosity, ownership, craftsmanship, and the drive to keep learning 

  • Good communication skills, able to explain trade-offs clearly to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders 

  • A good vibe: you bring energy to the team and make collaboration genuinely enjoyable, not just effective 

 

What We Offer You 

💶 Excellent remuneration, competitive and aligned with experience 

🌴 30 days holiday per year, with the option to buy 5 extra at half price  

🏦 Excellent pension contribution  

🎓 €1,000 education budget per year  

⏰ Flexible working hours, and location.  

🍱 On-site canteen (e.g., poke bowl for €2)  

🏋️ Free onsite gym- with personal trainer.  

🎉 A vibrant, open culture where you can be yourself  

🌿 Human- and values-driven work, not corporate bureaucracy  

🍻 Twice-weekly drinks on Thursdays and Fridays

title: Senior HR advisor / Senior HR Adviseur
description:
Maak impact op HR, organisatie en medewerkers

Wil jij als Senior HR Advisor complexe HR-vraagstukken vertalen naar praktisch en toekomstgericht HR-beleid? En krijg je energie van adviseren, verbeteren én zelf de handen uit de mouwen steken?

Bij Priva werk je nauw samen met onze HR Business Partners, HR Director en HR Operations-collega's. Je bent een ervaren sparringpartner voor het HR-team en de business en draagt bij aan complexe HR-casuïstiek, organisatieontwikkeling en strategische HR-projecten.

Je combineert een brede HR-expertise met een praktische aanpak. Van arbeidsrecht en verzuim tot HR-processen, beleid, data en systemen: jij weet wat er nodig is om onze HR-dienstverlening continu te verbeteren.

Wat ga je doen?

Als Senior HR Advisor:

  • adviseer je over complexe HR-vraagstukken, arbeidsrecht, verzuim, arbeidsvoorwaarden en organisatieveranderingen;

  • ondersteun je HR Business Partners en management bij individuele en collectieve HR-casuïstiek;

  • draag je bij aan strategische HR-projecten rondom onder andere cultuur, organisatieontwikkeling, transformatie en HR-beleid;

  • vertaal je HR-strategie en wet- en regelgeving naar duidelijke en werkbare processen en oplossingen;

  • werk je samen met HR Operations aan een professionele en efficiënte HR-dienstverlening;

  • analyseer en verbeter je HR-processen en systemen;

  • zet je HR-data en technologie in om betere beslissingen en procesverbeteringen mogelijk te maken;

  • werk je actief met HR-systemen zoals AFAS en kijk je verder dan alleen de gebruikerskant om processen slimmer in te richten.


Wie ben jij? 

Je bent een ervaren HR-professional die gemakkelijk schakelt tussen strategie, advies en uitvoering. Je hebt een stevige inhoudelijke HR-basis, maar kijkt tegelijkertijd verder: waar kunnen processen beter, welke impact heeft een verandering op de organisatie en wat hebben managers en medewerkers nodig?

Je bent kritisch wanneer dat nodig is, praktisch wanneer het kan en weet verschillende stakeholders mee te nemen in veranderingen.

Daarnaast breng je mee:

  • een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding, bijvoorbeeld HRM, Human Resource Management, Bedrijfskunde of Arbeidsrecht;

  • circa 3 tot 6 jaar relevante HR-ervaring, bijvoorbeeld als Senior HR Advisor, HR Adviseur of in een vergelijkbare brede HR-rol;

  • gedegen kennis van het Nederlandse arbeidsrecht en sociale wetgeving;

  • ervaring met complexe HR-casuïstiek, zoals verzuim, reorganisaties en arbeidsvoorwaarden;

  • ervaring met strategische HR-projecten, beleidsontwikkeling of organisatieverandering;

  • het vermogen om strategisch te adviseren én betrokken te blijven bij de operationele HR-praktijk;

  • affiniteit met HR-technologie, HR-data, AFAS en procesoptimalisatie;

  • uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal;

  • beschikbaarheid van 32 tot 40 uur per week.

Wat bieden wij?
In cijfers:

  • Een bruto salaris tussen €4.000,00 en €5.000,00 (op basis van je ervaring);

  • Een gezonde balans tussen werk en privé vinden wij belangrijk: 30 vakantiedagen per jaar en de mogelijkheid om meer bij te kopen;

  • 8% vakantiegeld;

Voor je eigen duurzaamheid:

  • Maak gratis en onbeperkt gebruik van onze eigen sportruimte "The Box" op de Priva Campus, met diverse lessen in bijvoorbeeld CrossFit, Pilates en Spinning;

  • Deelname aan de pensioenregeling van Priva;

  • Opleidingsmogelijkheden via onze eigen Priva Academy.

Klaar om jouw HR-expertise in te zetten én écht invloed te hebben op hoe we HR binnen Priva verder ontwikkelen? Breng je strategische blik, praktische aanpak en verbetermentaliteit mee en bouw samen met ons aan een HR-organisatie die klaar is voor de toekomst.

title: Security Architect
description:
Are you a security specialist in the OT space looking to expand your expertise into cloud solutions? Are you a cloud security champion passionate about bringing your expertise into OT/IoT space? At Priva Product Development Organisation we are looking for the Security Architect who will shape the security of our products.  

  

Security Architect in Priva Product Development – Why this role matters 

At Priva, we develop hardware products and software services for horticulture and building automation. Seeing the importance of our products for our customers, we recognize the need to continuously keep these secure in the ever evolving, fast-paced world. The security requirements in our landscape span four different areas: 

  1. Physical/embedded device security. 

  1. OT (operational technology) network security. 

  1. OT network to Priva-hosted cloud services communications. 

  1. Priva's hybrid on-prem/multi-cloud platform applications security, including applications, infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines.  

What makes this role truly unique is that our products contain long-lived hardware components that our customers run for years. Engineering future-proofed security solutions and maintaining a security posture at existing sites across all these areas having wide range of varying implementations and security needs creates a great challenge and a great fun. 

As part of the architecture team, you will play a key role in shaping the future of Priva's portfolio offered on the global market. You define security standards, security practices and security designs for our products that are used in tens of thousands of buildings and greenhouses. You work across product, engineering, and operations teams to ensure security controls and adhered to, implemented and tested as you have designed these. That’s real impact. 

What you will be doing 

As a Security Architect, you have a very simple mission: you see to it that Priva's hardware products and software (cloud) services are secured against known and emergent threats in lines with the industry standards and practices. You build upon your strong background in securing device/OT networks, cloud applications, and engraining the security practices in the daily work of Agile teams to achieve consistent security posture across all Priva products, designs, and customer deployments. 

 As a security architect, you are trusted counterpart of Priva Security, Quality, and Compliance officer to define, review, and execute controls arising from ISO9001 and ISO27001 standards and internal initiatives. You are responsible for presenting the necessary evidence of Priva’s compliance with these controls to the auditors. 

  • Security standards, policies, and design patterns library 

  • Security architecture review process 

  • Risk register and residual risk acceptance documentation 

  • Periodic product security implementation reviews, including maintaining non-compliance register 

  • Defined requirements, products and work packages for security-focused projects with 3rd party service providers, reviewing and accepting their deliverables, and supervising the implementation of these deliverables in the Priva hardware products and software services. 

  • Regulatory compliance (IEC 62443-4, ISO 27001, ISO 9001 or other standard that may be applicable in specific geographies) 

  • Threat intelligence briefing relevant to OT/IoT threat landscape 

  • Designing, implementing, and reviewing security controls applied at major customer sites. 

Above all, this is a hands-on role – occasionally writing code is included. You connect the industry’s best practices, ISO standards, product vision with the daily work of the product team. As a security architect, you practice what you preach. You explain, coach, and show by example the implementation of security as Secure SDLC in the developer’s daily work.  

To succeed in this role: 

  • You are passionate about OT security; you have great interest in the application of our products in the field. You are curious to grasp how our products truly work for our customers to find the best balance between security, reliability, and cost. You share the opinion that "if I don't secure Priva’s applications, then no one else will". 

  • You identify and eliminate issues in the development cycle that can jeopardize the security posture. You know and can show by example how to "test securely as well as test security" 

  • You are a great collaborator who can be a valuable sparring partner with product managers to understand and refine customer's needs for security so that you define the right security designs for market segments. Engineering managers rely on your ability to steer security implementations within the product teams. 

  • You are comfortable designing products that our customers will be running for years; comfortable providing guidance to LCM activities for existing customers to update hardware and software components to continuously stay secure. 

  • You share the knowledge about security subjects; you explain why security practices exist and what they achieve in the long run. 

  • You can translate security designs into engineering specifications, appraise implementation designs, conduct code reviews. This role with a strong hands-on component, not just a pure governance role. 

  • You understand and can register, document, and communicate clearly risks and trade-offs between differen t project execution scenarios 

  • You have had hands-on experience implementing security designs using modern programming language and frameworks, and you are able to coach product teams to increase their secure coding maturity e.g. by running threat modelling workshops with the engineering team. 

  • You have vast experience with architecture roles with 3-5 years of experience specifically focusing on security. 

In addition, you have the following technical expertise: 

  • Proven track record across at least two of the three domains: OT/IoT/embedded security, network security, cloud security 

  • You are familiar with modern authentication and authorization frameworks (JWT, OpenID, SAML) and (REST) API security and protection approached 

  • ISO 27001 and IEC 62443-4 understanding at a working level 

  • Working knowledge with or excellent ability to apply the PKI and certificate lifecycle management at scale; also, with the vision how to implement this in OT/IoT deployment contexts 

  • Solid network security understanding: firewall policy, micro-segmentation, DMZ design for IT/OT boundaries 

  • Zero trust architecture principles 

  • Secure SDLC and DevSecOps tools and practices (think about OWASP, SANS25, Snyk, Black Duck, etc) 

  


The following competence is desired: 

  • OT/ICS protocols and architectures (such as BACnet Secure Connect, Modbus, DNP3, MQTT, AMQP) 

  • Embedded device security for industrial PCs, systems-on-chip, and microcontrollers: secure boot, hardware security modules (HSMs), TPM, secure enclave concepts, firmware & data signing, encryption 

  • Cloud security on at least one major platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP) 

  • Container and Kubernetes security 

  • Secrets management and key management systems (HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) 

  • Priva's technical stack is C#/C++/.NET and Angular. Experience implementing production projects with this stack is preferred, but not required if you are able to learn it quickly (based on your vast experience) 

What we offer you 

  

💶 Excellent remuneration — competitive and aligned with experience. 

🌴 30 days holiday per year, with the option to buy 5 more at half price. 

🏦 Excellent pension contribution. 

🎓 Education budget of €1,000 per year. 

⏰ Flexible working hours. 

🍱 Onsite canteen (e.g., poke bowl for €2). 

🏋️ Free onsite gym. 

🎉 Vibrant, open culture.

title: Legal AI Growth Manager

Founded in Norway and built for the legal profession from day one, we integrate with local legal sources across multiple jurisdictions and are currently available in 12 languages. As we grow, we're looking for someone at an unusual and valuable intersection: a legal professional ready to step into thought leadership, marketing, growth, and technology - and help us speak credibly to legal professionals while opening doors into the communities where they already gather.

Your role as a Legal AI Growth Manager

Building trust in the legal profession starts with understanding the people behind it. That's why we're looking for a legal professional who can help Saga build meaningful relationships, strengthen our presence in the Dutch legal market and connect with the communities where legal professionals exchange ideas and knowledge.

As Saga's first Legal AI Growth Manager, you'll join the Marketing & Growth team and work closely with Legal Engineering, Sales and Product. Why join Saga

Take your legal career in a new direction, without leaving your expertise behind.

You'll join an international team of lawyers, engineers, builders, and commercial professionals working to make legal AI genuinely useful and accessible. We keep structures light, encourage ownership and give people room to experiment, learn and make an impact.

description:

We're a smart hydration company rebuilding an industry that still runs on sugar water and single-use packaging.
Filtered water, functional flavors, zero bottles. Still, sparkling, cold, and hot. All poured from one tap. We create hydration people want to reach for, starting with the workplace where we help teams thrive.

Growing that fast and thriving comes down to our people. Our team is our biggest asset and one that we’re proud of. We’re committed to maintaining our vibrant culture as we continue to grow.

About the role

You don’t need to have been an engineer. You do need to want to ship code. You’ll report to our Head of Digital Product.


What you'll Do

  • Own the roadmap: prioritize by business value and user pain. Kill ideas that don’t earn their place.

  • Find the real problem: work directly with the teams who use AURA every day.

  • Build features yourself: go from idea to working feature with AI, not to a spec handed off to someone else.

bunch is building the backbone of private markets. We are enabling next-gen fund operations with one integrated system that combines secure data infrastructure, AI-powered workflows and expert fund services. Your primary responsibilities will be ensuring our engineering output delivers tangible customer value, setting technical and architectural direction, and developing the people and team capacity needed to deliver sustainably. You will help shape the next stage of our engineering organisation, with a focus on Product Excellence, clear ownership, and sustainable engineering processes.

Your Role

  • You will be at the core of building the technology that powers bunch: secure, reliable infrastructure that makes private-market operations simpler and more efficient.

  • You will lead a team and have full accountability for delivering solutions that truly solve customer problems, connecting engineering decisions to product outcomes.

  • You will help us scale beyond our Series B by strengthening our architecture, growing our engineers, and building delivery practices that support long-term quality rather than short-term output alone.

You will:

  • Collaborate with Product Management: Actively participate in problem discovery and solution creation, using your technical expertise to shape pragmatic solutions alongside Product and Design.

  • Own capacity management and delivery: Take a proactive role in planning, make priorities and trade-offs explicit, and own your team's output from discovery through release and follow-up. Balance customer impact, delivery predictability, and engineering quality.

  • Drive collaboration across teams: Work closely with other engineering teams and cross-functional partners to manage dependencies and ensure smooth delivery of new features and improvements.

  • Manage our architecture and technical debt: Guide system design, scalability, performance, and maintainability within your team's domain and across shared systems. Make deliberate investment decisions that keep our platform ready for growth.

  • Develop sustainable engineering practices: Establish clear quality standards and practical ways of working that help the team deliver reliably without adding unnecessary process.

  • Support team growth: Coach engineers through regular feedback and development conversations. Ensure they understand the core problems we are solving and how their day-to-day work contributes to customer outcomes and their own growth plans.

About you

  • 3+ years' experience leading engineering teams, with a track record of developing engineers and taking accountability for delivery.

  • A strong understanding of system design principles, scalability, and performance tuning, with sound judgment about architectural trade-offs and technical debt.

  • The ability to create structure in a growing organisation while keeping processes pragmatic and focused on outcomes.

  • Experience with private markets, fintech, highly regulated industries, or document processing is a plus.

Our tech stack

title: (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte (w/m/d) bei Dezernat Zukunft – Institut für Makrofinanzen
description:
Wer wir sind und was wir suchen

Ob die Energiewende gelingt, entscheidet sich nicht allein an Technologien, sondern an Kosten, Märkten und politischen Weichenstellungen. Genau dazu arbeitet das Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft – und um unsere Arbeit weiter zu vertiefen, suchen wir Dich. 

Das Dezernat Zukunft ist ein überparteilicher Berliner Think Tank an der Schnittstelle von Politik, Verwaltung und Forschung. Rund 30 Personen verfolgen gemeinsam das Ziel, Geld-, Finanz- und Wirtschaftspolitik neu zu denken und verständlich zu vermitteln. Geleitet von den Werten Würde, Wohlstand, Demokratie und Nachhaltigkeit suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt – idealerweise ab dem 1. Januar – für unser Energy Lab eine Person als (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte. 

In dieser Position konzipierst Du Analysen und Studien zu Energiemärkten – insbesondere zum Strommarkt – und führst sie eigenständig durch. Dabei betrachtest Du Energiekosten, Investitionsbedarfe, Gesamtsystemkosten sowie die Wechselwirkungen politischer Instrumente mit diesen Größen. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Fragen, wie sich Energiepolitik mit Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Nachhaltigkeit und Bezahlbarkeit zusammendenken lässt, wie Energiekosten strategisch und gezielt gesenkt werden können, und wie das regulatorische Umfeld so ausgestaltet werden kann, dass es den Erfolg der „zweiten Hälfte der Energiewende“ und damit die Erreichung der Klimaneutralität ermöglicht.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du analysierst Energiemärkte und -preise, einschließlich Systemkosten, und koordinierst dazu Forschungsprojekte. Dabei betrachtest Du auch fiskalpolitische Auswirkungen sowie Wechselwirkungen mit dem Stromnetzausbau. 
  • Du entwickelst konkrete Politikvorschläge, Analysen und Positionen zu den oben genannten Themen, in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Deinen Kolleg:innen im Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft sowie den weiteren Teams der Organisation. Außerdem organisierst Du Expert:innen-Gespräche und andere inhaltliche Veranstaltungen. 
  • Du interagierst aktiv mit Vertreter:innen von Parlamenten, Regierungen, Wissenschaft, Wirtschaft und Medien. Unsere Arbeit funktioniert nur dann, wenn wir mit diesen Gruppen im Austausch stehen, zuhören und zusammenarbeiten.

  • Aktive Unterstützung bei Deiner Weiterentwicklung – fachlich sowie in Bezug auf Kompetenzen, Netzwerke und Aufgaben. 
  • Einen Arbeitsplatz in Berlin-Mitte mit der Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten und gemeinsam vereinbarten Kernzeiten.
  • Unbürokratische, verständnisvolle Regelungen bei kurzfristigen Care-Bedarfen; bezahlte Freistellung nach § 29 TVöD bei persönlichen Anlässen (z. B. kranke Kinder). 
  • Einen Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket oder JobRad. 
  • Und nicht zuletzt: Ein dynamisches,motiviertes Team, gemeinsame Events (z. B. Berg- oder Paddel-Ausflüge) und Arbeit, die zählt. 


Dein Profil

  • Du teilst unsere Werte und Ziele, begeisterst Dich für Energie- und Klimapolitik und brennst dafür, dass die Transformation gelingt. 
  • Du hast einen Master-Abschluss in einem relevanten Fachgebiet sowie mindestens zwei Jahre einschlägige Berufserfahrung. Du kennst Dich in Energiemärkten – insbesondere im Strommarkt – aus, verstehst politische Instrumente und erkennst, welche Zahlen für politische Entscheidungen und ökonomische Weichenstellungen wirklich zählen. 
  • Du konzipierst und erstellst eigene Analysen – quantitativ wie textlich – selbstständig und gründlich. Du hast bereits erfolgreich Forschungsprojekte umgesetzt und Ergebnisse sowie politische Handlungsempfehlungen prägnant kommuniziert. Du bist Dir bewusst, dass unsere Analysen und Vorschläge in der Öffentlichkeit intensiv geprüft werden, und arbeitest entsprechend gewissenhaft und bist bereit, als Eigentümer:in für Deine Projekte einzustehen.
  • Du kommunizierst sehr gut in deutscher und englischer Sprache und verfasst in beiden Sprachen anspruchsvolle, gut verständliche Texte.
  • Du hast fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse in der praktischen Anwendung gängiger KI-Programme. 
  • Du willst den Dingen auf den Grund gehen und jeden Tag dazulernen. Noch wichtiger als mitgebrachtes Wissen ist für uns die Fähigkeit, es zu erweitern und Meinungen zu ändern. 
  • Du arbeitest gern im Team, hörst zu und unterstützt und förderst Deine Kolleg:innen.
Die perfekte Kandidat:in erfüllt nicht immer jede Anforderung. Wenn Du glaubst, dass Du zu uns passt – bewirb Dich gern trotzdem und sag uns, warum.


Beschäftigungsbeginn & Vertragsbedingungen

  • Beginn: Von uns aus so schnell wie möglich. Im Anschluss an das Bewerbungsverfahren rechnen wir mit einem Start im Januar 2027. Das genaue Startdatum ist verhandelbar.

Bewerbungsverfahren

title: Senior Compliance Manager – Quality & Regulatory Affairs / QMB ISO 13485 (m/f/d)
description:
Intro

Back problems are the most common reason for inability to work in Germany.

Vivira has the solution: digital exercise therapy via app – always available, simple, effective, and reimbursed by health insurance. Behind every application permanently listed in the DiGA directory stands a robust quality management system. That is exactly why we are looking for you: As Senior Compliance Manager, you will take on the role of Quality Management Representative (QMB) according to ISO 13485 and keep our medical devices MDR-compliant – from the next audit to the inclusion of further products in the DiGA directory.


Your responsibilities include

As Senior Compliance Manager (m/f/d), you will be responsible for our quality management system and take on the role of Quality Management Representative according to ISO 13485. You report directly to our Team Lead Compliance and work closely with Engineering and Product.

  • QMS & Regulatory Affairs: You monitor compliance with DiGAV, MDR, ISO 13485, and ISO 27001, contribute to our BSI certification topics, and develop processes, SOPs, and Work Instructions pragmatically and based on risk.

  • Technical Documentation: You create and maintain the Technical Documentation according to MDR (DHF/DMR) for our three medical devices – one app listed in the DiGA directory and two CE-marked products in DiGA studies.

  • Audits: You prepare and follow up on external audits with the notified body, and plan and conduct internal audits. Your first milestone: the ISO 13485 recertification audit in February 2027 – with a stable system, complete documentation, and a planned handover by your predecessor.

  • Releases & Post-Market Surveillance: You review and approve release documentation and are responsible for post-market surveillance of our products.

  • Supplier Management: You evaluate and monitor our software providers (e.g. Atlassian, HubSpot, Google) according to criticality.

  • Regulatory Radar: You evaluate regulatory changes monthly and derive concrete measures.

  • Interface within the Company: You are the primary contact for regulatory questions across all departments – from Doctor Success to Patient Success –, train colleagues, and proactively gather input.

Whether the role of PRRC (Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance) becomes part of the function will be discussed together during the selection process – depending on your qualification and a clear agreement on responsibilities.

The biggest challenge? Making regulatory requirements understandable across the company – explaining why something is necessary rather than just distributing guidelines – and actively engaging colleagues both in the office and remotely.


What you should bring

  • You have at least three years of relevant experience in the medical device field and know MDR and ISO 13485 from practical experience. You want to bring your QM/RA experience into a dedicated QMB role – or already bring it with you.

  • You have prepared, accompanied, and followed up on audits. Having independently managed an audit is a plus – as is experience with internal audits.

  • You bring genuine technical understanding: You know how software development works (frontend vs. backend, releases, tickets) without needing to code yourself. A background in hardware or implants is welcome if your tech affinity is right.

  • You are ready to assume the QMB role according to ISO 13485.

  • You work in a structured, thorough, and independent manner, actively approach colleagues, and follow up when input is missing. You can say "No, that won't work" – while simultaneously finding pragmatic, risk-based solutions that Engineering and Product can work with.

  • You have very good German skills (at least C1) to reliably understand and communicate German DiGA regulations, and very good English skills for collaborating with our engineering team.

  • A plus, but not a requirement: Experience with DiGA or Digital Health, SaMD (Software as a Medical Device), ISO 27001 / ISMS or BSI certifications, as well as knowledge of Confluence, Jira, or Matrix Requirements.


What to expect at Vivira

  • Ownership: You independently design the QMS – your own processes, high freedom, short decision-making paths.

  • Career Leap: Your own QMB responsibility covering a broad spectrum including MDR, DiGA, ISO 13485, ISO 27001, and BSI – built on an established system with a planned handover.

  • Workplace: Hybrid in Berlin with 1–2 days per week in the office. Travel occurs only occasionally (under 10%).

  • Working Abroad: Up to one month per year, you can work from within the EU, EEA, Switzerland, Israel, or the UK.

  • Recharge: 30 vacation days for true breaks.

  • Health: Our app for your own back health.

  • Securing the Future: Increased employer contribution to the company pension scheme.

  • Corporate Benefits: Exclusive benefits for shopping, tech, and more.

  • Referral Bonus: Every successful recommendation from your network is rewarded.

  • Highlights: Multiple company and team events per year – and a dedicated team.

Dein Profil

Das bringst du mit:

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

Cx App Foundations is a platform organisation within our global Cx organisation. It provides shared consumer foundations and platform capabilities used by engineering teams across Wolt, DoorDash, and Deliveroo. Within this organisation, the Velocity team owns the paved road for consumer app development across mobile and web: shared SDKs and client foundations, integration patterns and multi-brand customisation, migration playbooks and reference implementations, and developer tooling that makes building on shared foundations fast and safe. Our mission is to reduce the cost, time, and risk of building consumer experiences across platforms and brands. Product teams own customer-facing experiences; our job is to make sure they can spend their time on delivering delightful experiences. The team is AI-native: AI is a default part of how we design, build, and ship software.

About the Role

As the Engineering Manager, you will lead a team of experienced engineers across mobile and web, collaborating closely with product teams, design, and adjacent platform organisations across three brands. Your primary responsibility will be owning the team's roadmap and delivery of shared client foundations, and driving their adoption across the organisation, so that product teams ship delightful customer experiences without rebuilding the foundations under them. You will be a key player in keeping the team's operating model healthy: clear intake from stakeholders, predictable delivery, and support expectations that keep the platform from drifting into a general escalation queue. You will also guide architectural and system design decisions with your tech leads. You will stay hands-on: contributing code, reviews, and prototypes alongside the team is part of the job. This role is ideal for a leader who has run platforms, SDKs, or shared services for other engineering teams, communicates clearly across brands and time zones, and wants their impact measured through what other teams achieve with the foundations you ship.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Own the platform roadmap - the shared SDKs, client foundations, and developer tooling the team ships - and sequence it against the migration and adoption goals of the three brands
  • Drive adoption of the shared foundations by partnering with product teams, running onboarding and rollout support, and making the supported path the easiest path
  • Lead, coach, and grow experienced mobile and web engineers, keeping growth conversations, calibration, and feedback loops running
  • Keep the team's operating model healthy: clear intake (stakeholder management, shared-platform, product-specific, or exception work), supported capabilities with entry criteria and support expectations, and predictable delivery
  • Guide architectural and system design decisions for client foundations that three brands and multiple app platforms depend on
  • Stay hands-on by contributing code and reviews alongside the team, and champion AI-native development practices
  • Grow the team through hiring

 

Our humble expectations

  • You have 3+ years of experience managing engineers, including a team with senior engineers
  • You have a solid background (5+ years) in mobile or web engineering, with enough technical depth to hold your own in architecture discussions about client foundations
  • You use AI tooling fluently in your day-to-day work and stay close to the code
  • You have run a platform, SDK, or shared service that other teams depend on, and know how to treat internal customers as customers
  • You work across boundaries naturally: product teams, design, other platform organisations, data/analytics and stakeholders in other locations and time zones
  • You hold a high bar for engineering quality and can navigate production incidents and release tradeoffs with calm structure

What we offer

A platform leadership role with real leverage: the foundations the team owns shape how consumer experiences get built across Wolt, DoorDash, and Deliveroo, and your roadmap decisions multiply across every product team that builds on them.

Next steps

The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

The compensation will be a combination of monthly pay and DoorDash RSUs. The latter makes it exceptionally easy to be excited about our company growing and doing well, as you'll own a piece of the pie.

 

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

title: Senior Software Engineer (AI/Data)
description:
About Codat

Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.

Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.

The Role

We're building the Advisory Intelligence Platform: Codat's client intelligence delivered inside the assistant a banker already uses (Microsoft Copilot first). Ask it anything about a client and it answers from the client's real books. Don't ask, and it still tells you what's changed, why it matters and what to do about it. Under it we're building the semantic layer, so every answer uses the same definitions, the signal layer that spots what's changed for a client, and the reasoning layer, a Codat-side LLM that turns those signals into advice. The first bank goes live this year. You'll be building the data and reasoning behind all of it.

This is a hands-on job for software engineers who want to build the systems a model reasons over, not configure a warehouse. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS. The product lives inside the AI assistant our clients already use, and we build it the same way: agents do the repetitive work, engineers do the hard parts. You'll build it and you'll run it. Nobody hands it over the wall once it's live. You'll also get a real say in where it goes next. That means making your case to engineers, product and the commercial team, and bringing them along with you.

What You'll Work On

  • The semantic layer. Measures, dimensions and definitions the model is allowed to use, so every answer it gives is the same answer. Yours to grow, persona by persona.

  • The signal layer. Detecting what's changed for a client and surfacing it before the banker asks. You'll be designing and building this.

  • The reasoning layer. A Codat-side LLM that turns signals into advice. Our calculations are the ground truth it reasons over. You own the calculations the model relies on, and the names, definitions and structure that let it pick the right one.

  • The agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers behind the assistant. What tools it has, how they're built, how they fail, and the evals that prove they work.

  • Everything from raw source data to the number the assistant quotes: the pipelines, services and data models, with the testing and observability to prove the number is right and the evals that catch the model quoting the wrong one.

You'll Probably Have

  • Built production systems from scratch, writing the code yourself rather than configuring managed services. You think about interfaces, failure modes and how the next person will change your code. If we ask about the hardest system you've built, you'll have a story ready.

  • Served data to an LLM and seen where it goes wrong: ambiguous definitions, poor retrieval, no evals. You know why "the model will work it out" isn't a data strategy.

  • Worked with data along the way, and liked it. You may never have been called a data engineer. You've built things that move, shape and serve data, and you know how they break, and how a model breaks on top of them.

  • Solid C#, Python or another backend language. Your code comes with tests, and you leave things tidier than you found them.

  • Depth in at least one of SQL, Spark, Databricks/Delta Lake, Dagster/Airflow/Temporal or dbt. Bonus if you've shaped any of them into something a model can query, through a metrics layer, metric views or an MCP server.

  • Time with CI/CD, Docker, cloud infrastructure (we're on Azure) and observability. Even better if you set them up for a team.

  • An interest in the business behind the data. If someone asks for a number the data can't support, you'll say so, and you'll build the guard-rail so the model says so too.

  • Treated your own workflow as something to engineer. AI has already taken over the repetitive parts of it, and you're the person others ask how to do the same.

How We Work

We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.

There’s no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don’t want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

A World-Changing Company

The Role

Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team.
