People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and produt. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them , keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow.

The opportunity

We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products, not bolted at the end.

As our hands on compliance adviser in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

Compliance advisory is the heart of this role and will take around 70% of your time. You’ll also pick up a smaller, complementary slice of work as our Data Protection Officer (DPO), around 30% of your time. DPO experience is a plus but not essential, and we’ll train you if you need it.

What success looks like

In your first year, compliance advisory is where you’ve made your mark. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. You’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

Alongside that, in the smaller DPO part of your role, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand.

To do this you'll be involved in:

Compliance advisory (around 70% of your time)

  • Product development: turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start.

  • Product lifecycle management: keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures.

  • Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.

  • Marketing: working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged.

  • Service (Operations): building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use.

  • Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.

  • Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.

  • Working with second line (Protect): bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge.

Data Protection Officer (around 30% of your time - training will be provided if needed)

Being our DPO means:

  • advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs)

  • monitoring how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other global data protection laws and our own policies

  • training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection

  • being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data

As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data.

We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

We need a proactive compliance doer first and foremost. You get stuck in without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable tackling regulations you haven’t met before. You use your experience and expertise to help our teams find simple, clear and compliant solutions. Your advice is balanced, easy to follow and focused on the risks that matter most. You want to push the business forward, and you see good compliance as part of how we get there.

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

  • Compliance experience in the first (preferred) or second line of a UK regulated firm, ideally a bank, e-money institution or payments firm.

  • Practical knowledge of the rules behind our products, like Consumer Duty, BCOBS, CASS, FISMA, the Payment Services Regulations and the Money Laundering Regulations. As well as familiarity with HMRC requirements like BBSI and AEOI reporting.

  • Hands-on experience turning regulation into practical requirements for product, sales or operations teams.

  • An openness to picking up data protection as part of the role: a genuine interest is enough, DPO experience isn’t required.

  • A curious, questioning approach. You know the right questions to ask before signing something off, not just the rules to check it against.

  • The confidence to challenge, clearly and kindly, when something isn’t right.

  • A love of writing. We have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write).

Ideally, you would also:

  • Have deep expertise in at least one specialist area, such as payments, cards, Consumer Duty, BCOBS, financial promotions or similar.

  • Have been a DPO, or worked closely with one, in a regulated firm.

  • Have worked in finance or banking.

What can we offer you?

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

  • Salary: £ 80-90 (DOE)

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. How long will the process take?

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We’re remote-first

We trust people to do great work wherever they are. We hire across the UK and most of our team works remotely full-time. We have a small London office in Moorgate for those who want it, and about a third of the company is close enough to use it occasionally, but there's no expectation to be there. At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. title: IT Project & Delivery Management Consultant (Early Career)
description:
Kickstart your consulting career where technology and business meet. Do you have a passion for IT and business?

As an ITPDM Consultant at Valcon, you will help clients achieve their strategic goals through innovative IT solutions and lead the way in digital transformation.

Taken

What will you do?

At Valcon, we don’t just implement technology. We redefine how businesses operate with it. As part of our IT Project & Delivery Management (ITPDM) capability, you will create and deliver applications, processes, insights, and automation solutions that leverage modern cloud platforms. By aligning business and IT, you will help our clients achieve their strategic objectives and drive meaningful change.

Your week as an ITPDM Consultant is dynamic and varied. You might spend one day at the client’s office, running workshops to align business needs with IT solutions. Another day, you could be analysing data and collaborating with your team at Valcon HQ or working from home to prepare reports and refine solution designs. Every few weeks, you join a collaboration day at the Valcon office to connect with colleagues, share updates, and learn from each other. Throughout the week, you’ll engage with stakeholders, contribute to project deliverables, and help drive impactful IT strategies.

Your responsibilites will include (but not be limited to):

  • Transforming business needs into innovative IT solutions by crafting user stories and intuitive designs.
  • Analysing and improving business processes to drive digital transformation.
  • Supporting the delivery and implementation of IT solutions, from concept to completion.
  • Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to ensure successful project outcomes.
  • Managing IT delivery projects in agile, hybrid, or traditional environments.

Each project brings unique challenges, giving you the opportunity to develop a broad skill set and make a real impact. Whether you’re facilitating workshops, aligning business and IT, or optimising processes, your work will contribute to achieving the client’s strategic goals.

Vereisten

Experience:

  • A curious and eager-to-learn mindset; you look beyond the obvious.
  • 2 to 8 years of relevant work experience in roles such as business analysis, IT consultancy, or project management.
  • A bachelor’s or master’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Business Administration, Information Management, or Computer Science).
  • Affinity with IT and technology, such as application development or low-/high-code solutions.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to engage with various stakeholders.
  • Fluent in Dutch and English, both written and spoken.
  • Experience with agile working is a plus.

Benefits

What do we offer you?

  • Personal development: a tailor-made growth path with training, courses, certification and mentoring by experienced colleagues.
  • An innovative work environment: collaborate with a team of experts pushing boundaries in data, technology, and consulting.
  • Immediate impact and responsibility: you’ll make a difference for our clients from day one and are entrusted with responsibilities that challenge you to bring the best out of yourself.
  • Inspiring work culture: a supportive, flexible, and no-nonsense environment that fosters your growth and fully allows you to be yourself.

Additionally, we offer:

  • Competitive employment benefits, including bonuses and expense allowance.
  • A company car or mobility budget.
  • A workplace that prioritizes and respects your work-life balance (for example by offering you the option of taking a sabbatical or expand the amount of holidays per year).
  • An affordable sports membership that allows you to participate in 50 different sports offered by over 10,000 partners.
  • The opportunity to work remotely from abroad for 10 days per year.
  • A vibrant community that organizes both professional and social events.

Ready to apply?

Has the above sparked your interest and are you ready to join our innovative and impactful environment? And do our core values – Together, Joy, Curious, Can do, and Integrity – resonate with you?

Our recruitment team would be happy to hear from you! Please apply directly to schedule a coffee meeting at our office first.

title: Financieel Controller die het verschil maakt (Beek en Donk)
description:
Ben jij een gedreven financieel professional met oog voor detail en procesverbetering? Heb je ervaring in het beheren van een financiële administratie en ben je klaar voor een rol binnen een groeiend familiebedrijf? Dan zijn wij op zoek naar jou! Coppelmans Ontstoppingen en Reinigingen B.V. (C.O.R.) is op zoek naar een Financieel Controller die de financiële processen naar een hoger niveau tilt en ons helpt bij het realiseren van verdere groei en innovatie.

Wie zijn wij?
Coppelmans Ontstoppingen en Reinigingen B.V. (C.O.R.) is al meer dan 40 jaar een betrouwbare specialist in het verhelpen van rioolverstoppingen, rioolreiniging, rioolreparatie en het vernieuwen van afvoersystemen. We werken voor diverse klanten, zoals woningbouwverenigingen, het bedrijfsleven, aannemers, overheidsinstellingen en de particuliere sector in voornamelijk Noord-Brabant en Limburg.

Sinds vorig jaar heeft de oprichter het stokje overgedragen aan zijn zoon en dochter. Met een frisse blik en een vernieuwde aanpak, zijn we bezig met verjonging en modernisering van onze organisatie. Je komt te werken in een hecht team op kantoor, waar een mix van medewerkers van verschillende leeftijden (20-60 jaar) samenwerkt. Samen zorgen we voor het succes van onze organisatie.

Taken

Wat ga je doen?
In de rol van controller ben je verantwoordelijk voor de financiële administratie en het beheer van een actuele en betrouwbare boekhouding. Jij fungeert als het financieel geweten voor de directie en krijgt volop de kans om verbeteringen door te voeren in automatisering en financiële processen. Samen met de financieel medewerkers zorg je voor een juiste- volledige- en tijdige administratie. Daarbij heb je een breed takenpakket, waarbij je jouw expertise in zet om onze financiële processen naar een hoger niveau te tillen.

De belangrijkste taken zijn:

  • Beheren van de financiële administratie, inclusief rapportages, belastingaangiften en jaarrekening.
  • Ontwikkelen van rapportages, KPI’s en BI-dashboarding voor betere financiële prestaties.
  • Analyseren van financiële prognoses en businesscases ter ondersteuning van bedrijfsbeslissingen.
  • Optimaliseren en automatiseren van administratieve processen.
  • Samenwerken met collega’s bij het ondersteunen van verwerken salarissen, loonbelasting en btw-aangiften.
  • Je bent dé persoon binnen de organisatie als collega’s financiële vragen hebben.
  • Je geeft zowel gevraagd als ongevraagd advies aan de directie over marktontwikkelingen, trends en visies om het bedrijf te helpen groeien.
  • De missie en visie van het bedrijf omzetten naar concrete doelen.

Vereisten

Jouw profiel
We zoeken een gedreven financieel controller die proactief meedenkt met het bedrijf en financieel inzicht combineert met een scherp oog voor detail. Je hebt een zelfstandige werkhouding en bent een teamspeler. Je bent analytisch sterk en beschikt over een hands-on mentaliteit. Je voelt je verantwoordelijk voor het verbeteren van financiële processen en kunt dit op een gestructureerde en accurate manier uitvoeren.

Wat wij zoeken:

  • Een bachelor diploma in Bedrijfseconomie, Accountancy of vergelijkbare richting.
  • Sterk analytisch inzicht en de vaardigheid om financiële processen te beheersen.
  • Uitstekende kennis van Excel en affiniteit met IT-processen en automatisering.
  • Een professionele werkhouding en sterke communicatieve vaardigheden.
  • Ervaring met het uitvoeren van financiële analyses en het maken van rapportages.
  • Kennis van Exact Online is een pré.
  • Een contract voor maximaal 32 uur.

Benefits

  • Veel verantwoordelijkheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief.

title: Adviseur Loopbaan en Mobilteit
description:
Als je goed zorgt voor je mensen, zorgen zij goed voor jou. Deze overtuiging van de oprichter van ADG Dienstengroep vormt de basis van Koersmakers. Koersmakers is een nieuw bedrijf dat werkt aan duurzame inzetbaarheid voor vakmensen, zodat zij maximale regie krijgen over het (werkende) leven. Om dit goed in de praktijk te brengen zijn we op zoek naar een adviseur in de regio Amsterdam/Rotterdam, Noord en Oost Nederland

Omschrijving van het team

Koersmakers is een jong, maar groeiend team van 9 collega’s. De mobiliteitsadviseurs Annemiek, Celine, Wilco, Miranda, Mariëlle, Dana en Inez, begeleiden ieder in hun eigen regio vakmensen in verschillende trajecten: van spoor 2 re-integratie tot (loopbaan)coaching en van gespreksbegeleiding tot leiderschapstrainingen. Zwaantje ondersteunt hen in de dagelijkse operatie en Sterre is kwartiermaker en eindverantwoordelijk voor Koersmakers.

Taken

Wat ga je doen?

Als adviseur ga jij in de verschillende trajecten de verhalen, doelen en talenten van hun vakmensen naar boven halen. Op dit moment begeleid je hoofdzakelijk medewerkers in een Spoor 2 re-integratie traject. Tegelijkertijd worden we inmiddels ook steeds vaker gevraagd om vakmensen te begeleiden in (loopbaan)-coaching trajecten en bij gespreksbegeleiding. En die beweging naar preventieve dienstverlening omtrent de inzetbaarheid van vakmensen is precies de stap die ze de komende tijd samen met jou willen zetten.

In de begeleiding van vakmensen maak je gebruik van passende (interesse)testen, waaronder de Predictive Index. Jij zet vervolgens dat wat iemand wil, drijft en kan, om naar concrete acties om de inzetbaarheid van deze vakmensen te vergroten en behouden. Hierbij houd je rekening met de actuele regels tot Wet Verbetering Poortwachter en de verzuimcyclus van het UWV. Daarnaast ondersteun je de leidinggevenden van de verschillende ADG bedrijven hoe zij samen met hen de regie van vakmensen op het (werkende) leven naar de praktijk kunnen brengen.

Ze vinden het geen probleem als je geen tot weinig ervaring hebt met het gebruik van onze testen.

Vereisten

Wat ze wel belangrijk vinden:

  • Je hebt ervaring met het uitvoeren van Spoor 2 re-integratie trajecten.
  • Je vindt het leuk om te werken aan de duurzame inzetbaarheid van hun medewerkers. Vakmensen die werk doen wat vaak niet gezien wordt, juist als het écht goed gedaan wordt. Schoonmaakmedewerkers, onderhoudsmonteurs, hospitality professionals, BOA’s en zorgmedewerkers. Zij houden Nederland draaiend. Zij doen het voor hén.
  • Jij zorgt dat de uitvoering van hun dienstverlening (in geval van Spoor 2 re-integratie) voldoet aan de eisen die de verzuimcyclus en de Wet Verbetering Poortwachter stelt.
  • Je legt makkelijk contact met andere mensen, ook in onbekende situaties. Je toont interesse in wie zij zijn en kunt een leidende en sturende rol goed afwisselen met een luisterende en afwachtende rol.
  • Je werkt zelfstandig, beschikt over probleemoplossend vermogen en neemt regie over de trajecten die je begeleidt. Je schakelt gemakkelijk met verschillende gesprekspartners en vertaalt doelen naar concrete stappen, ook wanneer de situatie nog niet volledig duidelijk is
  • Je werkt gericht toe naar (nieuwe) mogelijkheden voor vakmensen om (weer) inzetbaar te worden en blijven. Je vertaalt doelen en mogelijkheden in concrete afspraken en houdt jezelf, medewerkers en leidinggevenden aan deze afspraken.
  • Jij blijft je, ook bij weerstand of uitdagingen, inspannen om de inzetbaarheid van vakmensen te vergroten of behouden.
  • Je werkt precies en zorgvuldig en signaleert bij onvolledigheden en afwijkingen in de begeleiding of rapportages. Hierbij schroom je niet om te benoemen wat je ziet en hoort, durf je kritische vragen te stellen, altijd met het doel om tot oplossingen en mogelijkheden voor inzetbaarheid te komen en altijd met respect voor de ander.

Benefits

Dit mag jeverwachten

  • Een maandsalaris van EUR 3500 tot EUR 4500 op basis van 40 uur
  • Een jaarcontract voor 24 tot 40 uur
  • 27 vakantiedagen op basis van 40 uur
  • Een dertiende maand
  • Opleidingsmogelijkheden, denk bijvoorbeeld aan:

o De predictive index practitioner

o Of een andere opleiding die bijdraagt aan de doelstelling van Koersmakers: regie over het (werkende) leven naar de praktijk brengen.

  • Een fijne werkplek in Houten of bij een van onze ADG zusjes.
  • Mogelijkheid om thuis te werken.
  • De kans om echt impact te maken en mee te bouwen aan een nieuw bedrijf

Over Koersmakers

Koersmakers is een startup van ADG. Een Twents familiebedrijf met ruim 11.000 collega’s dat groot is geworden met en dankzij hun vakmensen op de werkvloer. ADG zet zich in voor vakmensen met waardering en ondersteuning.

Bij Koersmakers geloven ze in gelijke kansen voor iedereen en in een open organisatie waar iedereen zich prettig voelt. Zij willen dan ook een diverse en inclusieve werkgever zijn. Inclusie zorgt ervoor dat werknemers, ongeacht hun achtergrond, overtuigingen, voorkeuren etc, zich gewaardeerd, gerespecteerd en betrokken voelen. Koersmakers gelooft dat dit leidt tot een creatievere en productievere werksfeer, waar innovatieve ideeën kunnen bloeien, betere besluiten worden genomen en talenten volledig tot hun recht kunnen komen.

title: Medior Pensioen Consultant
description:
Wil je aan de slag als consultant binnen een dynamische omgeving waarin eigen ontwikkeling centraal staat? Wil jij samen met ons in teams werken aan oplossingen voor complexe financiële en maatschappelijke vraagstukken? Mercer is per direct op zoek naar een medior pensioenconsultant voor onze vestiging in Amstelveen of Rotterdam.

De afdeling Pensioen (Wealth) is verantwoordelijk voor dienstverlening aan pensioenfondsen en werkgevers, waaronder strategische advisering, certificering, ALM en diverse pensioenvraagstukken. Het gaat om een veelzijdige en dynamische rol voor een professional die kennis heeft van het reilen en zeilen binnen het vakgebied pensioen. Als consultant ben je onderdeel van een of meerdere klantenteams. Je begeleidt en controleert ook junior collega’s bij het uitwerken van pensioenvraagstukken en ondersteunt de senior collega in het uiteindelijke adviestraject richting de klant. Je bent van start tot finish bij de opdrachten betrokken en speelt een belangrijke rol in het projectmanagement binnen het klantteam. Naast het werk voor de klant ben je onderdeel van specifieke kennisgroepen en heb je de mogelijkheid je te ontwikkelen tot expert op deelgebieden. Je bent onderdeel van de totale Wealth afdeling, die bestaat uit een jong en ambitieus team van ruim 60 professionals.

Taken

  • Analyseren van klantvragen en klantbehoeften en op maat gemaakte adviezen voorbereiden, samen met het klantteam.
  • Zelfstandig uitvoeren danwel controleren van actuariële berekeningen en analyses.
  • Voorbereiden van rapporten, presentaties en adviesmemo’s.
  • Je onderhoudt contacten met pensioenuitvoerders & andere relaties
  • Je bent in staat kleine tot middelgrote (deel)projecten zelfstandig te coördineren
  • Het begeleiden van junior consultants en het ondersteunen van senior consultants. Jij bent de spil in het team.
  • Bijhouden van de relevante actuele ontwikkelingen in het pensioenveld en deze toepassen in je werk. Continu leren en verbeteren kenmerkt deze rol.
  • Het up to date houden van diverse documenten en bestanden.
  • Managen van je eigen werkvoorraad en planning en proactief bijdragen aan de team doelen.
  • Verdiepen van kennis op deelgebieden (expert rol).

Vereisten

  • In het bezit van een HBO of WO diploma
  • Je hebt 2 - 5 jaar relevante werkervaring
  • Je beschikt over uitstekende analytische en rekenkundige vaardigheden.
  • Je bent klantgericht, adviesvaardig, communicatief sterk, proactief en een teamspeler.
  • Goede beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal in woord en geschrift.

Benefits

  • Afwisselende en uitdagende opdrachten met relevantie voor de top uit het zakelijke segment en voor grote beleggers zoals pensioenfondsen.
  • Uitstekende doorgroeimogelijkheden.
  • Een competitief salaris.
  • Goede concurrerende secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden.
  • Ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling en training.
  • Platte hiërarchie, open-deur-cultuur en ruimte voor persoonlijk initiatief.
  • Aandacht voor werk-privé balans.

Mercer is een mondiale aanbieder van advies op het gebied van Health, Wealth en Career. Bij Mercer bevorderen we de gezondheid, welvaart en carrières van meer dan 110 miljoen mensen. Dit doen wij door werkgevers te faciliteren bij het maken van weloverwogen keuzes. De 20.000 Mercer consultants, verspreid over meer dan 170 kantoren in 43 landen, bieden de klant ondersteuning bij het oplossen van complexe vraagstukken ten aanzien van arbeidsvoorwaarden en menselijk kapitaal, en bij het ontwerpen en beheren van ziektekostenregelingen, sociale voorzieningen en pensioenen. Zo helpen wij onze relaties een goed werkgever te zijn en zorgen wij vandaag voor de dag van morgen.

Onze fundamentele waarden vind je terug door heel Mercer - in de verschillende kantoren en regio's, bedrijven en oplossingen, generaties en culturen. Meer dan 28.000 bedrijven en hun werknemers over de hele wereld werken samen met en groeien door Mercer, omdat wij geloven in:

  • Mensen zijn het hart van alles. Ze drijven onze innovatie, onze oplossingen, en onze passies.
  • De toekomst wordt gemaakt door de acties die we vandaag nemen. Samen hebben wij de kracht om morgen gezonder, gelukkiger en meer de moeite waard te maken.

Dit doel verenigt onze collega's over de hele wereld, en deze principes weerspiegelen onze inzet voor de individuen en gezinnen van wie wij het leven dagelijks beïnvloeden.

title: Werkstudent (m/w/d) für die 3D-Datenaufbereitung
description:
aurivus ist ein innovatives Startup, das sich auf die Entwicklung einer hochmodernen KI zur 3D Datenverarbeitung in Web-Anwendungen spezialisiert hat.
Inspiriert von den erfolgreichsten Softwareunternehmen der Welt haben wir eine starke Software- & KI-Entwicklung in Ulm aufgebaut.

Zur Unterstützung unseres Teams suchen wir engagierte Werkstudenten (m/w/d) für die 3D-Datenaufbereitung.

Aufgaben

3D-Daten-Labeling in Blender:

  • Identifizieren und Markieren (Labeln) unterschiedlicher Elemente in 3D-Modellen.

  • Nutzung eines eigens entwickelten Blender-Addons zur Vergabe der Labels.

  • Dokumentation der gelabelten Daten und Prüfung auf Vollständigkeit und Richtigkeit.

  • Rückmeldung zu Funktionalität und Benutzerfreundlichkeit des Addons, ggf. Mitwirken bei der Optimierung des Workflows.

2D-Raumpläne nachzeichnen:

  • Überprüfung der Nachzeichnungen auf Genauigkeit und Konsistenz mit den Vorlagen.

  • Eigenständiges Erkennen und Nachfragen bei fehlenden Informationen oder Unklarheiten in den Plänen.

Allgemeine Unterstützung:

  • Zusammenarbeit mit dem Entwicklungsteam und Kommunikation über den Status, Herausforderungen und mögliche Verbesserungen.

  • Zusammenstellung und Pflege einfacher Dokumentationen zum Label-Prozess und den genutzten Methoden.

Qualifikation

  • Eingeschriebener Student (m/w/d)

  • IT-Affinität und Begeisterungsfähigkeit für neue Technologien

  • Selbstständige, strukturierte und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise

  • Teamgeist und Kommunikationsstärke

  • Idealerweise erste Erfahrungen mit der Arbeit mit Blender

Unsere Aufgaben sind vielseitig. Begeistere uns mit deinen vielseitigen weiteren Erfahrungen und Fähigkeiten.

Benefits

Das Beste an einem Startup ist, dass man mit guten Leuten zusammenarbeitet.

  • Die Möglichkeit, an einem spannenden Produkt im KI-Bereich zu arbeiten, das sich stark auf 3D-Visualisierungen und Datenauswertungen fokussiert.

  • Einen modernen und gesunden Arbeitsplatz mit höhenverstellbaren Schreibtischen, großen Bildschirmen und Sitz-Steh-Hockern

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiteinteilung mit bis zu 20 Wochenstunden

  • Die Tätigkeit erfolgt in Präsenz in unserem Büro im Science Park in Ulm

  • Wir vergüten deine Leistung mit einem Stundenlohn von 15,00 €

  • Wir bieten Startup-Feeling mit kurzen Kommunikationswegen

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung – ganz egal, welches Studienfach du belegst oder in welchem Semester du bist!

0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers.

Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes:

  • Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses.

  • Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity.

description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 10x YoY.

The Role

We’re looking for an AI Ops Engineer to build the internal systems that help Kernel scale without adding unnecessary manual work. You’ll work across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations - finding the highest-leverage problems and building practical AI-powered workflows.

This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll take ideas from a vague business problem to a tool or workflow that people use, then maintain and improve it in production. You’ll choose the fastest sensible approach for each problem - coding agents, automation platforms, APIs, data pipelines or lightweight code.

You’ll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations, and partner closely with GTM, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define how an AI-native company operates: help build Kernel’s internal playbook for using AI across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations

  • Make our GTM team more productive: automate the repetitive work in prospecting, account research, meeting prep and CRM hygiene, so BDRs, AEs and Account Managers spend more time with customers

  • Build internal tools and workflows: use coding agents, APIs, automation platforms, no-code tools or lightweight code

  • Turn company data into operational leverage: connect and improve data across our systems, then put it to work in AI agents, proactive workflows and better decision-making

  • Put AI agents to work across Kernel: give teams agents with the right context, tools and guardrails so they can move faster without sacrificing judgement or reliability

  • Be Kernel’s own internal customer: deploy Kernel on Kernel’s CRM, improve our GTM data and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering

  • Level up the team: help colleagues become confident AI users, document what works and turn successful experiments into repeatable ways of working

Your First 6 Months

For your first six months, you’ll focus on our sales team. You’ll sit with our BDRs, AEs and Account Managers and learn how they work day to day. Then you’ll automate everything that doesn’t need a human. That means going deep on Salesforce and our GTM stack, and owning the RevOps workflows behind them. After that, you’ll bring the same approach to Marketing, Customer Success and Operations.

What You Bring

  • A track record of shipping: you’ve built tools, automations or AI workflows that people use every day, ideally inside a small, fast-moving startup. Around 2–5 years of experience is typical, but what you’ve built matters more than your years. Ex-founders welcome

  • Experience inside a high-growth startup, or building your own, is highly desirable

  • Curious about sales: you’re keen to learn how our BDRs and AEs work, and how Salesforce is set up, before you build for them

  • AI-tool obsessed: you are constantly testing new models, agents, MCPs and workflows, and you have the judgement to turn them into reliable systems that people actually adopt

  • Strong data instincts: you can turn fragmented, messy information into reliable workflows and create feedback loops that keep it trustworthy

  • Can’t unsee inefficiency: you see the company as a connected system; when you find a broken or unnecessarily manual process, your instinct is to understand it, build the fix and make sure it sticks

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

  • Prefer deep specialization over breadth: this role means switching between projects and teams, depending on business needs

  • Prefer steady-state work over project-based sprints: priorities will shift as the business evolves

  • Only want “strategic” work: you will personally build the tools, clean the data and fix the workflows

❌ This role is definitely not for you if you:

  • Need every task to be clearly scoped before starting: ambiguity and learning on the fly are constant

  • Avoid operational grunt work or lose interest after the prototype

  • Want to protect a 9-to-6 or a mostly remote setup: we are in the office together 4–5 days a week and the pace is high

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 💰 Salary: £60,000–£85,000 + equity

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🥕 £450 monthly office dinner allowance

  • ✈️ 2 weeks work-from-anywhere

  • 🍼 Generous parental leave policy

  • 💼 Pension plan

  • 💻 Top-spec equipment and central London office

  • 🎉 Team events and dinners

  • 🚀 Work directly with the founders to deploy AI across a fast-growing company

  • 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

❤️ Team

Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations

Amin Shafi, BizOps Associate

Dave Bentham, Head of Sales

Not offered for this role.

  • Stage 2: Technical - In-person case interview

  • Stage 3: Coffee chat - In-person discussion with members of our GTM team

  • Final Stage: Values - Interview with founders for culture and values alignment

If there is mutual fit, we move to references and offer.

Who is Atominvest

Atominvest is the operating system for modern private markets asset managers. Our modular, flexible SaaS technology underpins key investor- and portfolio-management workflows.

Our customers are sophisticated private equity, growth equity, and private credit firms managing billions in assets globally. We aim to deliver ongoing high-quality outcomes for them through a long-term partnership mindset.

At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

About the role

Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself.

You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one.

 

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

 

You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works.

As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today.

It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on.

The machine that builds the product

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.

I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.

That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.

Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.

You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.

What you'll do

Build the machine that builds the product

Most of your time goes here.

  • Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

  • Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

  • Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.

Own the platform

  • Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

  • Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

  • Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.

Work across the stack

  • Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

  • Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

  • Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.

Your first six months

  • Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

  • At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

  • Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients.

  • Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

  • Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.

How you'll work

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.

You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.

This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.

You'll probably enjoy this if

  • You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one.

  • You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it.

  • You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team.

  • You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster.

  • You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week.

  • You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so.

This probably isn't for you if

  • You want a pure DevOps or SRE role.

  • You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible.

What you'll bring

Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you.

  • Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda.

  • Infrastructure as code as a habit, with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code.

  • Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt.

  • Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's.

  • Security and compliance as part of engineering: least privilege, secrets management, and evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

  • Production experience: on-call, incidents, post-mortems, and observability tooling such as Datadog, Grafana or Honeycomb.

  • Full-stack product building. Senior TypeScript and Node.js, plus React, with a track record of shipping features end to end yourself, not just supporting the people who do.

  • Test automation and CI/CD. You've designed pipelines that test at the right levels and release safely, and you keep them fast and simple.

  • Tooling you've built for AI agents, not just used: agent configuration and orchestration, MCP servers or similar integrations, evals, automated review.

Our stack

TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.

How we hire

We want to see how you actually work, so there are no whiteboard puzzles.

  1. Screening call with me (20 minutes)

  2. Competencies interview with me (30 minutes)

  3. Technical deep dive with a few of our engineers (90 minutes)

  4. Culture fit interview with our CEO, Hemal (30 minutes)

I'll be your main point of contact throughout. You'll know what to expect before each stage, and if we don't make an offer, I'll give you feedback.

title: Senior Field Marketing Manager, EMEA
description:
About Assembled

Assembled helps companies scale great customer support. As consumers, we’ve all been there. You need help, you’re stuck on hold or going in circles with an AI, and your problem still isn’t solved.

Behind great support is a complex operational problem: thousands of people and AI agents working across teams, time zones, and products as new problems emerge. Assembled gives support leaders the tools to manage that complexity, from AI agents that resolve customer issues to software that forecasts demand, builds schedules, and makes intraday adjustments.

More than 400 companies, including DoorDash, Salesforce, Stripe, and Sephora, trust Assembled. We've raised $71M from NEA, Emergence Capital, Stripe, and Basis Set Ventures and have offices in San Francisco, New York, and London.

The Role

We’re hiring our first marketer in London. Europe is our next growth market, and right now we’ve got a tight-knit, quota-focused sales team with big goals and not much regional marketing behind them—yet.

 

You’ll change that. Field events are the engine — dinners, roadshows, conferences, executive gatherings that put our team in front of the CX and Workforce Management leaders running Europe’s most complex operations. But this isn’t a role that stops at the event calendar. You’ll be the person who figures out what the European market needs from marketing and then goes and does it.

 

We’re starting in the UK with plans to expand across the region. You’ll work closely with our global events lead on moments where EMEA shows up inside the worldwide program, and with our growth team on campaigns that need European flair.

 

We work together in person five days a week from our London office in King’s Cross.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own the EMEA field calendar and the budget behind it — decide which events, dinners, and roadshows are worth doing, and which ones we skip

  • Run field as a pipeline channel: pre-event targeting through opportunity creation and deal acceleration, with named accounts attached to every program

  • Build account-based programs sized to the deal, whether that's one account, a handful, or a roomful, in lockstep with the London sales team

  • Build our EMEA partner and channel motion — joint events, co-marketing, and the relationships that get us in front of buyers we can't reach on our own

  • Be the voice of the European market inside Assembled: what needs localizing, which content doesn't land, where our story has to change by country, and what customer stories to bring to life

  • Foster community efforts. Get to know the European CX/WFM community by genuinely contributing and building relationships across a wide variety of stakeholders

  • Bring EU-specific campaign ideas to the team and make sure Europe is designed into campaigns rather than translated at the end

  • Build AI workflows that let one marketer cover multiple countries — invite list enrichment, event pages, personalized follow-up at volume, post-event analysis

 

What You Bring

  • 6–9 years in field, events, or regional marketing at B2B companies selling into enterprise, including time owning UK or EMEA programs rather than supporting someone else's

  • Startup, get sh*t done mindset. The region is new and our team there is small and scrappy. You know how to spot the highest-leverage opportunities and collaborate cross-functionally to make magic happen

  • You've been early somewhere — the first marketer in a region or on a small team, where no playbook existed and you wrote one

  • Event judgment with receipts. Tell us about an event you cut and why, not only the ones that worked

  • Nice to have: experience in European markets beyond the UK, with an understanding of how programs need to differ by market

  • A close working relationship with sales. You've sat in pipeline reviews, you know what an AE needs from a dinner, and you can hold your own on account strategy

  • AI systems you've built and use, with an example you can walk through. One marketer covering this much ground without AI is a headcount request, not a plan

  • A bias to go first. You'd rather run a twelve-person dinner next month than spend the quarter planning a conference booth for next year

 

Our UK benefits

  • Quarterly credits for professional development, wellness, and commuting

  • Budget for AI tools and experimentation, giving you room to test new ideas, build workflows, and rethink how you work

  • Paid parental leave

  • Onsite work model with catered lunches everyday (M-F)

 

The estimated base salary range for this role is £80,000 - £105,000 per year. The base pay offered may vary depending on location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Stock options are provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position offered.

 

We know great candidates don’t always meet every requirement listed in a job description. If the role excites you and you believe you can make an impact at Assembled, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and are committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels like they belong and has the opportunity to do their best work. We look forward to hearing from you!

title: Sales Operations Business Partner
description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We’re looking for a Sales Operations Business Partner to sit between our sales leadership and the systems, data, and processes that run the revenue engine. You’ll help the sales team understand where deals stand, where revenue is coming from, and where it’s at risk. You’ll own how we track pipeline, report on performance, and build the dashboards leaders rely on to make decisions. This is a role for someone who thinks in business outcomes first and uses data and tools as the means to get there.

What you’ll do

  • Own pipeline management processes, including stage definitions, forecasting cadence, and hygiene standards, and work with sales managers to keep the pipeline accurate.

  • Build and maintain regular sales reporting covering bookings, pipeline coverage, conversion rates, win/loss, and rep and team performance.

  • Design, build, and maintain dashboards that give leadership and frontline managers a clear view of performance against targets.

  • Act as a business partner to sales leaders: understand their priorities, translate them into operational requirements, and bring data-backed recommendations to planning and business reviews.

  • Support forecasting and quarterly business reviews by preparing the data, challenging assumptions, and flagging risks early.

  • Own day-to-day administration and configuration of the CRM (e.g. Salesforce or HubSpot), including fields, workflows, user access, and reporting structure, in partnership with the RevOps or systems team.

  • Drive adoption of CRM and sales processes by working with managers and reps, and by making the right behaviour the easy one.

  • Support territory, quota, and compensation-related analysis as needed, in partnership with Finance.

  • Identify process gaps and inefficiencies across the sales funnel and lead improvements, documenting changes and training the team on them.

  • Work cross-functionally with Marketing, Finance, Customer Success, and Product Ops to keep data consistent across systems.

What you’ll bring

  • 7+ years of experience in sales operations, revenue operations, GTM operations, or a related commercial role, ideally in a [B2B SaaS / relevant industry] environment.

  • Strong experience with CRM systems, ideally Salesforce or HubSpot, including reporting and basic administration.

  • Solid understanding of sales metrics and funnel dynamics, including pipeline coverage, conversion, forecasting accuracy, and sales cycle length.

  • Proven ability to build clear reports and dashboards in tools such as Excel/Google Sheets, Looker, Tableau, or Power BI. You don’t need to write code, but you should be comfortable working with data and spotting what matters.

  • Experience running pipeline reviews or forecast calls, or supporting leaders who do.

  • A consultative approach: you can listen to a sales leader, ask the right questions, and turn their needs into a practical solution.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to present findings clearly to senior stakeholders and explain trade-offs simply.

  • Good judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to balance speed and accuracy.

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities.

Nice to have

  • Experience supporting a sales team through a scaling or transformation phase.

  • Familiarity with sales compensation or territory planning tools.

  • Exposure to revenue analytics or forecasting methodologies.

  • Experience with a BI tool or basic SQL, though this is not required.

What success looks like

  • Leadership trusts the pipeline and forecast numbers and uses them to make decisions.

  • Sales managers run their reviews from the dashboards you’ve built, without needing manual reports.

  • CRM data quality improves measurably over time.

  • Sales leaders see you as a partner who brings ideas, not just reports.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

title: Product Engineer | Design Engineering Knowledge
description:
Product Engineer | Design Engineering Knowledge

Location: Cambridge (UK), hybrid with up to 2 remote days per week

Team: Product

Start date: ASAP

About Neural Concept

Neural Concept is the engineering intelligence platform used by leading manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, and energy. We combine geometric and physics AI with LLM-based agents so engineering teams can move from customer requirements to validated designs in a fraction of the usual time.

About the role

Design decisions depend on information that lives outside the CAD model: customer requirements, design rules, manufacturing and assembly constraints, and cost targets. This information is spread across specification documents, handbooks, ERP systems, requirements management tools, and system models. Engineers gather it by hand, often late in the process, and conflicts surface at design reviews or on the production line.

We call the capability that closes this gap Design Engineering Knowledge. It connects the design to the information ecosystem around it, so requirements, constraints, and trade-offs are available to engineers and AI agents while they work on the design itself.

As a Product Engineer, you will build this capability. Requirements are the first focus area: extracting them from customer specifications and requirements management systems, structuring them, and keeping them traceable. You will then extend the same foundation to design rule checks, Design for Manufacturing (DfM), Design for Assembly (DfA), and Design for Cost, and connect it to the enterprise systems where this knowledge already lives.

You will work with the Product Manager, solution engineers, and customer engineering teams, as the primary developer from the first customer conversation to the version running in production.

What you will do

  • Build the requirements foundation: ingest customer specifications and RFQ packages, extract requirements with LLM and agent-based pipelines, and keep each one traceable to its source document and page.

  • Extend this foundation to design rules, DfM, DfA, and Design for Cost, turning standards, handbooks, and company know-how into constraints that software and agents can use.

  • Bring requirements, constraints, and trade-offs into the design workflow, so engineers can check a design against them at any stage and see which ones apply to the part they are working on.

  • Build integrations with the systems around the design: requirements management systems, ERP (cost, materials, and supplier data), and system design and MBSE tools for architecture and system-level requirements.

  • Design the data model that links requirements, rules, and constraints to parts, design parameters, and simulation results.

  • Create evaluation sets and quality metrics with customers, so extraction and checking accuracy is measured and improves with every release.

  • Design human-in-the-loop review flows where engineers validate and edit AI output, with versioning and a full audit trail.

  • Spot recurring patterns across customers and turn them into reusable components of the Neural Concept platform.

Who you are

Must have

  • Experience building and shipping production Python software in fast-moving, cross-functional teams.

  • Hands-on experience with LLM applications in production: structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, and evaluation.

  • Experience integrating with enterprise systems through APIs and data models, for example ERP, PLM, or requirements management tools.

  • Experience with document processing, such as PDF parsing, OCR, or information extraction.

  • Strong software practices: testing (pytest), CI, packaging, code review, and git.

  • A product mindset. You talk to users, understand the problem before writing code, and ship in small, measurable steps.

  • Clear, concise communication with both customer engineers and internal teams.

  • Based in Cambridge (UK) or willing to relocate.

Nice to have

  • Background in mechanical engineering or physics, with exposure to DfM, DfA, or design-to-cost practices.

  • Familiarity with requirements engineering and model-based systems engineering (MBSE, SysML).

  • Experience working with CAD data or geometry processing.

  • Experience with vision-language models, vector databases, or search ranking.

What you get

  • Ownership of a product capability that customers use in real engineering programs, with direct access to the engineers who use it.

  • A competitive salary and rewarding opportunities as we continue to scale.

  • A collaborative, multicultural team where your work is visible and recognized.

  • Colleagues who share knowledge freely and support each other.

  • A hybrid model and flexible hours. We focus on results and trust you to organize your time.

We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment where you can thrive.

title: Fractional Product Lead - 3 month contract
description:
We're customer obsessed. We put the customer at the heart of everything we do - and we're looking for people who feel the same way.

About Bike Club

Bike Club is the easiest way to keep kids on the right sized bike. Through our subscription model, we remove the hassle of buying, outgrowing and reselling children's bikes, so families always have the right bike, right when they need it. We are a purpose led, fast-growing business built on ease, care, progress and joy - with a relentless focus on customer growth, retention and building a more circular approach to children's cycling.

Role Summary and Engagement

Bike Club is looking for a fractional Product Lead to lead the member product, turn customer needs and commercial priorities into a clear direction and a prioritised roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements. The role combines senior Product leadership with practical discovery and delivery coordination in a lean team.

The Product Lead will also establish an AI-enabled Product function, using AI to speed up customer insight, discovery, prototyping and experimentation. They will identify where AI and automation can improve the member experience or business efficiency, and turn the strongest opportunities into prioritised, measurable initiatives.

This is a part-time fixed-term employment or freelance contract estimated at 3 days per week for a period of 3 months.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product direction and roadmap: own the direction and roadmap across the member lifecycle: joining, managing a subscription, ongoing membership, exchange and retention. Balance member value with operational efficiency, cost and business priorities.

  • Discovery: lead discovery with members and colleagues across Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and markets. Use research, behavioural data and service insight to define problems before committing to solutions.

  • Lifecycle and retention: work jointly with Marketing and the retention owner on lifecycle journeys, retention initiatives, experiments and shared measures. Product owns the supporting experience and requirements. Marketing owns campaign and channel execution.

  • Requirements and backlog: turn agreed priorities into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria. Maintain one prioritised product backlog, including operational improvements and approved AI or automation initiatives.

  • Investment cases: build proportionate cases for investment, setting out expected benefits, cost, dependencies and how outcomes will be measured. Recommend stopping or deferring work where value is insufficient.

  • Delivery: agree delivery commitments with Engineering using realistic estimates and available capacity. Coordinate stakeholders, adoption and launches with the combined QA and Delivery role, keeping risks and changes visible.

  • Marketing autonomy: support Marketing with appropriate content, landing-page and experimentation capabilities. Agree the boundary between the member product, CRM and support tools.

  • AI in Product work: use AI routinely for research synthesis, analysis, requirements development, prototyping and experiment design, and validate findings against customer evidence.

  • Prioritise valuable applications with Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and the Data and Automation function. Test assumptions and build proportionate business cases. Customer-service automation should support the wider member journey.

  • Share responsibility with Marketing for using AI to support lifecycle insight, proposition testing and retention experiments, with agreed measures of customer and commercial impact.

  • Leave things in a better state: because the engagement is part-time and time-limited, document the roadmap, backlog, ways of working and AI approach so the team can continue without the Product Lead, and hand over clearly at the end.

Requirements

  • Extensive Product Management experience including owning a digital product roadmap and delivering measurable customer and commercial improvements, preferably in a subscription, membership or related consumer business.

  • Strong discovery skills, including customer interviews, journey mapping, data interpretation, problem definition and testing assumptions before investment.

  • Commercial judgement: can compare value, effort, cost and risk, build practical investment cases and make clear prioritisation decisions.

  • Ability to lead across functions, challenge senior stakeholders constructively and maintain focus when priorities compete.

  • Experience working with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Customer Service and Operations through delivery, launch and continuous improvement.

  • Demonstrable experience embedding AI into Product workflows, with examples of faster learning, better decisions or reduced effort. Able to distinguish valuable AI applications from features that add unnecessary complexity.

  • Track record of working independently and effectively in a part-time, fractional or interim capacity, making visible progress in limited days a week.

  • Able to start quickly, and leave behind clear documentation and repeatable ways of working.

Measures Of Success

Baselines, numerical targets, data sources and review dates are agreed with the executive sponsor and relevant business owners within the first 30 days. Delivery and outcomes are reviewed weekly.

  • Member retention: improvement in the agreed retention or cancellation measure for targeted journeys, assessed jointly with Marketing and the retention owner.

  • Member experience: improvement in self-service completion and reduction in avoidable support contact for prioritised journeys, without deterioration in customer experience.

  • Conversion: improvement in agreed joining and exchange conversion measures, using experiments or comparable cohorts where practical.

  • Speed of learning: reduced time from identifying a customer problem to testing a solution, with evidence that decisions remain grounded in customer insight.

  • AI and automation: validated initiatives deliver agreed improvements in member experience, retention or operational efficiency, measured with the relevant business owner.

  • Roadmap value: proportion of priority initiatives with a stated outcome, baseline and measurement plan before delivery, followed by a documented benefits review.

  • Delivery confidence: performance against jointly agreed milestones, with changes in scope, priorities and dependencies recorded and communicated early.

Our Values

We look for people who live our values every day:

Ease: we make things simple for our members and for each other.

Care: we look after our customers, our colleagues and our bikes.

Progress: we keep improving, learning and raising the bar.

Joy: we help kids fall in love with cycling, and enjoy the work we do.

Why Bike Club?

You'll be joining a business with a clear purpose, a genuinely different proposition and significant opportunity to grow.

This is a rare opportunity to build the operating system for our national refurbishment and distribution site from the ground up, shaping how Bike Club gets the right bike to every family, right when they need it.

About WPP Production

We are WPP Production - the unified global production company that brings together all of WPP's content producers, studios and craft experts into one connected organisation. We combine world-class human craft with next generation technology to originate, design, and deliver multi-channel content systems at scale. About WPP

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world's leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com.

A Hybrid working model

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we've adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. description:

The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer.

Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service.

Pelagon is backed by Hexa, the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised.

title: AI Solutions Engineer
description:
Waarom deze rol bestaat

De meeste AI-projecten halen productie nooit. Zes maanden verder, budget verdubbeld, scope gehalveerd, en wat er ligt is een presentatie in plaats van software die eindgebruikers omarmen.

Wij doen het anders. Een werkende POC in zeven dagen, op echte data van de klant. Daarna in weken naar productie. Die belofte houdt alleen stand als de mensen die hem waarmaken scherp zijn.

Met agentic coding tools zoals Claude Code en Codex komt er sneller iets werkends uit dan ooit. Daardoor verschuift het werk van bouwen naar regie voeren. De vraag achterhalen, de juiste oplossing ontwerpen, AI en engineering slim inzetten, en de kwaliteit bewaken. Daarom zoeken we iemand die tussen developer en consultant in zit. Technisch sterk genoeg om zelf te bouwen en te beoordelen of iets deugt, sterk genoeg aan de voorkant om de vraag achter de vraag te vinden, en verantwoordelijk tot het live staat en live blijft.

AI schrijft bij ons veel. Verantwoordelijkheid kun je niet uitbesteden. Alles wat jouw naam draagt, heb je zelf gelezen, gecontroleerd en begrepen voordat het de deur uitgaat.

Taken

Er zijn twee manieren waarop onze klanten bij ons bouwen, en jij doet ze allebei.

Wij bouwen

Een klant stapt binnen met een proof of concept. Zeven dagen, een scherp gekaderde scope.

Jij ownt die POC. Jij vraagt uit wat er echt nodig is, jij bepaalt wat er wel en niet in gaat, jij bouwt hem op hun echte data, en jij neemt de klant stap voor stap mee in de demo. Daarna bouw je het in weken uit tot MVP. Vanaf dat moment doe je het niet meer alleen. Je haalt je team erbij, neemt ze mee in wat het moet worden en bouwt samen verder. Vervolgens maak je het productieklaar, met auth, monitoring en CI/CD. Jij blijft er eigenaar van.

De klant bouwt, wij borgen

Bij een groeiend deel van onze klanten bouwt hun eigen team met Claude Code, Codex en Cursor. Wij reviewen elke pull request, tekenen elke release en zetten de productieomgeving op, volgens onze standaarden en zonder dat ze erop hoeven wachten.

Je hebt je eigen klantportfolio en bent hun aanspreekpunt binnen SevenLab. Je begeleidt discovery sessies en workshops om tot richting en prioriteiten te komen, en je schat in wat je zelf doet, wat je samen oppakt en wanneer een specialist moet aanhaken.

Vereisten

Must have

  • meerdere jaren ervaring met het bouwen van webapplicaties of softwareproducten;
  • je hebt zelf software naar productie gebracht die nu live draait en door klanten wordt gebruikt, en je kunt het laten zien;

  • je kunt iets veilig live zetten en live houden: deployment, monitoring, security, en weten wat je doet als het misgaat;
  • je denkt in systemen. Kom je iets voor de derde keer tegen, dan los je het niet voor de derde keer op. Dan bouw je iets zodat het niet meer gebeurt;
  • je zoekt het eerst zelf uit in de documentatie, de code en de logs. Blijft er een vraag over, dan stel je hem met een hypothese erbij zodat de ander in één keer kan antwoorden;
  • je zet vaagheid om in richting, structuur en resultaat;
  • je communiceert scherp: je legt technische keuzes uit aan mensen zonder technische achtergrond, en je geeft feedback op andermans werk zodat ze er wat mee kunnen;

Nice to have

  • ervaring met release-governance als specialisme: approvals, signing, rollback;
  • ervaring in gereguleerde sectoren zoals zorg of de publieke sector;
  • open source bijdragen op je naam.

Voor wie dit is

  • je wil eigenaar zijn van het hele traject, van eerste gesprek tot wat er live staat, en je vindt het prettig dat het jouw naam is die eraan hangt;
  • snel en goed zijn bij jou geen tegenpolen. Je haalt dat door scope scherp te houden en te weten waar je niet op moet inkorten;
  • je wil voorop lopen, probeert nieuwe dingen uit en wil beter worden dan je gisteren was;
  • je denkt verder dan "kunnen we dit bouwen". Je vraagt je ook af wat het oplevert en wat de slimste route is;
  • als er iets stukgaat, ben jij degene die het meldt voordat iemand het vraagt.

Voor wie dit niet is

  • de developer die het liefst de hele dag in zijn editor zit en klantcontact vermijdt;
  • de consultant die adviseert wat een klant moet bouwen en daarna weg is. Wij zijn verantwoordelijk tot en met productie;
  • iemand die veel prototypes maakt die daarna blijven liggen;
  • iemand die de output van een chatbot doorstuurt zonder hem zelf te lezen. AI gebruiken doen we allemaal, de hele dag. Het ongelezen doorgeven van wat eruit komt is iets anders;
  • iemand die een vraag bij een ander neerlegt voordat hij de documentatie heeft opengeslagen of zelf heeft getest.

Waar je mee werkt

Fullstack JavaScript en TypeScript, Vue en Nuxt, PostgreSQL en Drizzle, Claude Code en vergelijkbare agentic tooling, CI/CD, monitoring. We draaien op NVIDIA-infrastructuur en op Scaleway voor Europese data-residency. We zijn ISO 27001-gecertificeerd en onze klanten zitten in sectoren waar dat niet vrijblijvend is.

Ons proces

Na je sollicitatie plannen we eerst een korte remote kennismaking. Daarna volgt een gesprek op kantoor met een praktische case of assessment.

In die case bepaal jij wat je zou uitvragen, wat je in en buiten scope zet om het af te krijgen, wat er niet deugt aan wat er ligt, en wat er moet gebeuren voordat dit veilig live kan. Je mag AI gebruiken zoveel je wil. We kijken ook naar de vragen die je ons stelt.

You will also be collaborating with Merchant Finance & Treasury to make sure they can do daily reconciliation in our BI tooling.

  • Flexibilität: Auch als Trainee genießt du bei uns flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit zum Homeoffice.
  • Internationale Luft: Durch unser Netzwerk von 28 Partnerbüros arbeitest du in einem wirklich globalen Umfeld.
  • Die Perspektive: Unser klares Ziel ist es, dich nach erfolgreichem Abschluss deines Traineeships als festen Junior Manager in deiner Spezialdisziplin in unser Team zu übernehmen.

Bist du bereit für diese Herausforderung?
