title: Post-doctorante ou Post-doctorant en Evaluation de la vulnérabilité d’un réseau d’accès Télécom de type PON (Passive Optical Network) vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS (Distributed Acoustic Sensor) - CDD de 12 mois
description:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 5 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons notre futur(e) post-doctorant(e) en évaluation de la vulnérabilité d’un réseau d’accès Télécom de type PON (Passive Optical Network) vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS (Distributed Acoustic Sensor) pour rejoindre le département Communications et Electronique (COMELEC).

Cette étude se situe dans le cadre du projet « Ecoute Acoustique Terrestre » (EAT) RAPID (Régime d’Appui Pour l’Innovation Duale), fruit d’un partenariat entre la société Febus Optics et Télécom Paris.

 La mesure de vibrations acoustiques distribuées par fibre optique (DAS, Distributed Acoustic Sensing) est une technologie récente, dont les applications ne cessent de se diversifier. On peut citer par exemple la détection d’intrusion en surveillance périmétrique, les mesures sismiques, le diagnostic de puits (pétrole, géothermie), etc. La bande passante de la mesure, de sub-Hertz à la centaine de kiloHertz, permet également d’envisager la captation de la bande audio, et donc de réaliser des mesures audios sur une fibre optique. Il est ainsi possible d’utiliser le réseau optique télécom d’un bâtiment pour réaliser des écoutes, en utilisant un système DAS modifié, intégrant des artéfacts matériels particuliers (enroulement, antennes, connecteurs) au voisinage de la zone d’écoute et un traitement du signal spécifique pour obtenir des performances suffisantes.

Le cadre de ce Postdoc est d’évaluer la vulnérabilité d’un réseau télécom vis-à-vis d’écoutes potentielles par DAS. Le branchement sur un réseau optique Telecom local en fonctionnement nécessite de s’adapter à son architecture, notamment en termes de plan de longueur d’onde.

L’audit des systèmes de télécommunication afin d’en évaluer la vulnérabilité constitue un enjeu majeur du réseau télécom. Un exemple de configuration d’un réseau d’accès est décrit dans la figure ci-après. Depuis le réseau Backbone, à partir du ‘Central Office’, les signaux télécoms sont acheminés chez les abonnés via le PON (Passive Optical Network). À l’intérieur des bâtiments, un réseau FTTX (Fiber To The X=H home, X=R room, X=O office, etc) ou un réseau local LAN (Local Area Network) optique servent respectivement à acheminer le signal optique jusqu’au terminal final ou à communiquer entre deux terminaux locaux via une liaison optique. Le PON comprend une fibre nourricière (Feeder Fiber) puis, au moins, un coupleur 1×N. Le codage de l’information est alors un mélange de multiplexage en longueur d’onde grossier (C-WDM) et de multiplexage temporel (TDM). Chaque voie de sortie du coupleur 1×N est envoyée vers des groupes de 1 à n abonnés à travers, au moins, un filtre qui sélectionne la longueur d’onde qui leur est allouée. Le signal après ce filtre est alors monochromatique et codé TDM. Le dernier coupleur 1×n répartie le signal chez les n abonnés. Ce PON comprend donc, entre autres, des coupleurs passifs qui divisent les signaux vers différents abonnés mais aussi des connecteurs, soudures, etc.

L’objectif de ce Postdoc est de faire un état des lieux des différents types de réseau mis en place et d’en évaluer les conséquences sur la capacité de mesures DAS :

·         Description des différents types de réseaux locaux existants,

·         Etats des lieux des différents types de transmission : CWDM, TDM, …

·         Quels sont les différents points d’accès pour une mesure DAS ?

·         Comment discriminer les différentes fibres interrogées après un coupleur ? Influence des points réflecteurs,

·         Etude des différentes marges de puissance pour une mesure DAS,

·         Potentielle présence de nœuds d’insertion et limite de la transparence optique,

·         Sensibilité des mesures DAS en fonction des différents types de fibre et de leur environnement,

·         Influence du réflecteur final sur la capacité d’écoute.

Le caractère innovant sera la définition des conditions du réseau et des configurations et des performances DAS permettant un audit cyber sur des infrastructures déjà déployées.

Au-delà d’une synthèse des configurations que l’on peut trouver sur le terrain, il s’agira de mener des tests, soit sur un réseau réel auxquels un accès nous sera donné, soit sur un réseau modèle implémenté pour l’étude. Ces travaux permettront d’identifier le type de modules d’interfaçage nécessaires, et de les spécifier, puis de les concevoir et de les fabriquer.

Vos principales missions seront :

  • Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine des capteurs à fibre optique distribués

  • Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

  • Participer à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris


Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat en génie électrique, en communications optiques, en photonique, en capteurs optiques ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez d’une solide expertise théorique et pratique en photonique et en traitement du signal numérique, ainsi que de bonnes compétences en programmation. Une connaissance des algorithmes de traitement du signal appliqués aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique, notamment dans le cadre de la détection cohérente, constitue un atout. Vous maîtrisez l’anglais, et la pratique du français est souhaitée.

Vous manifestez un intérêt marqué pour la recherche appliquée et êtes capable d’évoluer dans un environnement multiculturel. title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Data Engineer

Shiftbase is building the self-driving assistant for shift-based businesses across Europe. We want to take that work off their plate and eventually do it for them.

Underneath that product vision sits a data challenge. Insight, automation, and AI all depend on data people can trust, and the foundation for it doesn't exist yet.

You will build the foundation that fixes this.

What you'll do

  • Architect the warehouse. Design and own our BigQuery and Dataform warehouse from the ground up. Build a layered, well-modeled foundation, medallion staging through marts, not only the models that sit on top. Ask every day whether the whole company can trust and reuse it.

  • Make the data flow reliably. Build ELT and ETL with incremental, idempotent loads, orchestration, and retries, so pipelines run on time without anyone watching them. Ship monitored pipelines that hold up in production.

  • Take the transform layer. Own the Dataform model-building and transform layer, taking full responsibility for the transformation layer and freeing up capacity for semantic modeling and business definitions. This unblocks the whole team.

  • Build trust into the data. Make validation, freshness monitoring, alerting, and lineage the default. Diagnose failures at the root cause. leadscorev2 is the outcome this role exists to prevent.

  • Serve the whole company. Feed clean, governed datasets to Metabase, HubSpot, and the ML and AI work the product ML team owns. Push modeled data back into the tools business teams act on, including HubSpot and Customer.io.

  • Own the Platform handshake. Run the day-to-day collaboration with the Platform team on our GCP foundation, a bridge that only gets part-time attention today.

  • Treat the warehouse like a product. Keep documentation, lineage, and discoverability current so departments trust the data assets, and handle sensitive HR and workforce data to GDPR standards.

What success looks like in your first 3–6 months

  • The warehouse has a real foundation. The first vertical slice, our accounts model, ships with tests and monitoring.

  • You fully own the Dataform transform layer, creating capacity for semantic modeling and business-definition work

  • Pipelines run against a defined freshness SLA, and you catch breaks before stakeholders do.

  • Documentation and lineage cover what you own, and datasets that were stuck now flow to the teams that need them.


What we're looking for

You have built warehouse foundations yourself. You designed them rather than maintaining someone else's, with a track record in:

  • Designing layered warehouse architectures (medallion, bronze-silver-gold) and dimensional models (star and snowflake) that teams reuse

  • Advanced SQL as your daily working language

  • Hands-on BigQuery, since our stack is GCP

  • Building a SQL transform layer in Dataform, or strong dbt experience.

  • ELT and ETL with incremental, idempotent loads and real orchestration, scheduling, and dependency management

  • Data quality, testing, freshness monitoring, and lineage built in from the start

  • Python for pipeline code, scripting, automation, and API integration

  • Reviewable, repeatable change through Git and PR-based deployment

Nice to have, not required: another modern cloud warehouse such as Snowflake or Redshift; managed ingestion such as Airbyte; preparing data for ML, LLM, and agentic use cases; and familiarity with B2B SaaS metrics and HR or workforce data. English is our working language, and Dutch is not required.

This role isn't infrastructure engineering, ML or MLOps, or dashboard analysis. The Platform team owns infrastructure, the Product ML team owns ML, and the business teams own dashboards. It also isn't for someone who has only maintained a warehouse another person designed. You build the foundation properly, stay transparent about data quality and trade-offs, and treat the warehouse as a product for the whole company. title: Frontend Engineer
description:
About Shiftbase

We build workforce software that helps people get work done. More than 10,000 companies use our platform every month to plan shifts and track time, with less admin in the way.

We work from our Zoetermeer office with over 80 people and we grow every year. The culture is open and informal. You can push back on an idea regardless of title, and we change how we work when someone makes the case in retro.

About the role

You build frontend features that customers use the day you release them. You sit in a product team with backend, QA, design and product, and you take a feature from a rough product idea to a screen a planner can use without a manual.

Your time is a balance between working on features, bugs and resolving technical debt.

Claude Code is how our engineers write software. Everyone here uses it daily, and whole features now go out with an agent doing most of the coding. You still own what you merge, so you read the diff, you know why it works, and you can defend it in review. The interesting part of the job is deciding what to hand to an agent, what to write yourself, and what context the agent needs to get it right the first time.

You ask what a planner is trying to do before you read what the ticket says. You automate the parts of your own process that don't need a human.

Year one, in order

First, ship. Deliver features in scheduling and time tracking. Start small, then take one full feature from the product conversation through to release.

Then, own an area. Pick up a product surface end to end and become the person the team asks about it, including what it should do next. That covers how AI fits your area, which patterns you document for the agent and which calls you keep for yourself.

Along the way, make what you build safe to change. Restructure and test the paths you build on while you build on them. Extend test coverage where it's lacking. We move fast and keep quality up by automating what a human doesn't need to do, including the checks that catch what an agent got wrong.

What you'll do

  • Design and build frontend features starting from rough product ideas

  • Deliver features with Claude Code, from the prompt through to the pull request, and review the output as closely as a colleague's

  • Write the patterns, conventions and project context our agents work from, so generated frontend code lands in the right shape

  • Turn tangled domain rules into screens people can use without a manual

  • Fix bugs in your own features and in code you've never seen

  • Improve the code you touch while you touch it, so the next feature in that area costs less

  • Write and maintain automated tests in Jest and Playwright

  • Ship in short cycles with your product team

  • Pair, review, and teach what you know

How we work

Frontend in Angular, backend in PHP, a web app and a mobile app in React Native. Tests in Jest and Playwright. We develop AI-assisted with Claude Code as the primary tool, and a growing share of our code starts there. Human review and engineers owning what they ship keep it safe. We ship in short cycles in product teams with mixed specialisations. We pair often, with each other and with an agent open. Every quarter you get time to build and ship one of your own ideas, and we run hackathons.




Must-haves

3+ years of professional experience with an SPA framework, Angular preferred. Depth in React or Vue works if you can show you'll carry it over.

You ship. You've delivered features to real users at a steady pace, and you can tell us what you cut to get them out.

You've shipped production code with an AI agent. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or similar. Tell us where you let it run, where you took the keyboard back, and what you changed about your own workflow after a month of it.

You automate your tests. Jest and Playwright, or equivalents, and you have an opinion about what deserves a test.

You simplify. Hand you a tangled domain problem and you produce a screen that hides the tangle.

You explain your choices. In review, in a design discussion, and to a product manager who doesn't read code.

You work as a peer. You pair, you review, and you make the people around you better without needing a title to be heard.

Nice-to-haves

  • Claude Code in particular, or agent setups you've tuned for a team rather than yourself

  • TypeScript at depth

  • Storybook or component library ownership

  • React

  • TDD

  • PHP, or enough backend to reason about the API you're consuming

  • Familiarity with a complex, regulated domain (ours covers scheduling, time tracking, leave, and labour law across countries)

This might be your dream job if…

✅ You want your work in front of customers within days

✅ You'd rather own a feature end to end than take a finished spec

✅ You want a say in how a team writes frontend code with agents while the answer is still open

✅ You improve the code you touch without being asked, and you stop before it turns into a six-week rewrite

✅ You like a domain that takes months to learn

This probably isn't your dream job if…

⛔️ You want the technical approach decided before the ticket reaches you

⛔️ You want a job where AI stays out of your editor

⛔️ You'd merge agent output you can't explain in review

⛔️ You'd stop shipping to finish a refactor

⛔️ You prefer pixel work and would rather leave tests and architecture to someone else

⛔️ You'd rather work alone than pair and review

description:

Wat ga je doen?

Als Account Executive voor de Nederlandse markt ben jij de persoon die kansen omzet in betalende klanten.

Je bedient de B2B-markt over de volle breedte: van horeca tot retail, van zorg tot transport. Bedrijven die vaak nog met Excel of een verouderd systeem werken en waarbij jij in één demo laat zien hoeveel tijd ze terugkrijgen. De use case is herkenbaar, de waarde is snel duidelijk en dat maakt je verkoopcycli lekker kort.

Het grootste deel van je pipeline is warm. Onze marketing levert continu leads aan van bedrijven die actief op zoek zijn, en dat gaat hard. Maar we willen niet afhankelijk zijn van alleen wat er binnenkomt. Je krijgt de ruimte, en de verwachting, om zelf ook kansen te creëren in accounts die je interessant vindt. Hoe we dat als team het beste aanpakken, bepalen we samen. Jouw ervaring in de praktijk weegt daarin mee.

Het volledige sales process is van jou, van discovery en demo tot onderhandeling en close. Na de close draag je het account over aan ons Customer Success-team. Jij focust volledig op new business. Je werkt met tempo en volume, en je weet wanneer een deal aandacht verdient en wanneer je hem moet laten gaan.

Je dag bestaat voor een groot deel uit bellen en demo's, want dit is een hands-on salesrol. Sporadisch ga je op pad naar een klant voor een persoonlijk gesprek.

Je bouwt mee aan een groeiend salesteam binnen een snelgroeiende organisatie, en dat vraagt energie, initiatief en doorzettingsvermogen. Je deelt wat voor jou werkt met het team, want we worden hier beter van elkaar.


Wie ben jij?

Een salesprofessional met een paar jaar ervaring die energie krijgt van tempo, van veel gesprekken en van scoren. Je hebt bewezen dat je kunt presteren in een snelle SaaS-salesomgeving en je wilt nu een volgende stap zetten in een team dat hard aan het opbouwen is. Je wacht niet tot de telefoon gaat: als je een account in gedachten hebt, vind je zelf een weg naar binnen.

Verder herkennen we je aan het volgende: je hebt minimaal 2 jaar ervaring in high-velocity software sales (SaaS), je bent commercieel scherp zonder je klant uit het oog te verliezen, je bent leergierig en staat open voor coaching, en je beheerst Nederlands uitstekend. Engels is een pre.

Profielen die ons aanspreken: je komt uit de SaaS-wereld en hebt ervaring met snelle funnels en hoge volumes. Denk aan omgevingen zoals Lightspeed, Zenchef of vergelijkbare SME-gerichte hospitality- of retailtech.

Of je hebt een leidinggevende achtergrond in de horeca, bent tech-savvy en hebt slimme techoplossingen geïmplementeerd in die rol, en je wilt nu de overstap maken naar software sales aan onder andere de horeca. In beide gevallen: je snapt de wereld van onze klanten als geen ander.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Een rol waarin je een SaaS-oplossing verkoopt die bedrijven écht vooruit helpt, in een omgeving waar resultaat en plezier hand in hand gaan.

Groei is hier geen loze belofte. We investeren serieus in je ontwikkeling vanaf dag één. Je start met een gedegen 30-60-90-dagen-onboardingprogramma met duidelijke milestones, zodat je precies weet waar je staat en waar je naartoe werkt. Je wordt daarnaast getraind en gecertificeerd via Winning by Design, hét toonaangevende salestrainingsprogramma voor SaaS, inclusief SPICED-certificering. Daarbovenop krijg je een persoonlijk ontwikkelbudget van €1.000 per jaar om te investeren in wat jou verder brengt: cursussen, conferenties, boeken of coaching. Jij kiest.

Verder bieden we een brutojaarsalaris van €55.000 tot €75.000 inclusief vakantiegeld op basis van 40 uur per week, afhankelijk van je ervaring. Daarnaast 25 vakantiedagen, een flexibele regeling voor thuis en op kantoor werken, een goede pensioenregeling en reiskostenvergoeding (NS Business Card of kilometervergoeding).

De werksfeer? Ontspannen, met gratis lunch, bootcamp op donderdag, vrijdagmiddagborrels en kwartaal-BBQ's.

Hoe werken we samen?

De eerste 3 maanden verwachten we een hogere aanwezigheid op kantoor in Zoetermeer. Logisch: je wilt het team, het product en de klant snel doorgronden, en dat gaat nu eenmaal sneller als je er bent. Na je onboarding werken we meer hybride.

Woon je op maximaal anderhalf uur reisafstand? Dan verwachten we je minimaal één keer per week op kantoor, op dinsdag of donderdag. In de praktijk gaan we hier flexibel mee om zodra het vertrouwen er is. Woon je dichterbij of heb je geen probleem met wat meer reistijd? Elke dag op kantoor is natuurlijk ook gewoon mogelijk. Daarnaast is er de hub in Amsterdam waar je terecht kunt.

Waarom Shiftbase?

Je verkoopt geen vaag platform dat niemand begrijpt. Shiftbase is marktleider in Nederland en groeit hard in Duitsland. Een product dat 10.000+ bedrijven dagelijks gebruiken omdat het hun werk simpelweg makkelijker maakt. Tegelijkertijd zijn we geen logge olietanker. Met 85+ collega's ben je geen nummer, want wat jij doet heeft directe impact op de koers van het bedrijf. Maar we zijn wél groot en stabiel genoeg om je een serieuze carrière te bieden. Geen start-up-roulette, maar een bewezen business met internationale groeiambities waar jij onderdeel van wordt.

title: Lead Analytics Engineer
description:
Do you love turning messy business questions into data people can trust? Can you connect the customer journey from the first marketing touch through sales conversion, revenue, retention, and product usage and explain the numbers equally clearly to an engineer, a CMO, and a CFO? AIHR is looking for a Lead Agentic Analytics Engineer to become the hands-on functional lead of our two-person Data & Analytics team. You will own the translation of cross-functional business questions into trusted metrics, governed semantic models, and decision-ready agentic analytics; set the analytical direction; and build the most critical models yourself. You are transforming raw data into governed products that drive decision-making for our business partners.

 

About AIHR

Founded in 2016 with the mission to future-proof HR, the Academy to Innovate HR (AIHR) has become the global market leader in online training for HR professionals. We support customers in more than 140 countries, including organizations such as Unilever, Reckitt, Goldman Sachs, Philips, Deloitte, Nike, Heineken, and UBS. Our goal is to continuously upskill and empower one million HR professionals.

Today, we are an international team of more than 100 people representing over 30 nationalities. We are driven by excellence, innovation, and a hunger to grow, while staying friendly, enthusiastic, and committed to helping each other succeed.

Working at AIHR means taking real responsibility, improving how we operate, and getting the freedom to develop in new areas and shape your role as the company grows.


Role and Responsibilities

AIHR's Data & Analytics team is part of Business Operations. You will work alongside Vahid, our Senior Data Engineer, and report to Leo, our VP of Business Operations. Our ingestion and warehouse foundation is largely established: data from systems such as HubSpot and our own LMS moves through ETL pipelines into Snowflake. Through special Projects, we are building governed semantic layers on top so the business can self-serve trusted analytics through Power BI, Metabase, and AI tools.

Your role owns the step that matters most: translating a business question into a clear definition, a well-designed model, and conversational/agentic analytics that your leadership trusts. You will set the analytical architecture, dbt standards, and roadmap, while Vahid focuses on ingestion, warehouse reliability, and engineering implementation. You will both build: you will personally deliver the most critical business models, review implementations, and ensure the outputs are usable by the business.

This role has no direct reports. Your colleague, Vahid, remains managed by the VP of Business Operations, while you have clear functional decision rights over metric definitions, semantic-model design, analytical quality, dbt standards, and technical priorities. It is designed for someone who wants to lead through expertise while remaining close to the work.

 

What You'll Own

  • Own and execute a rolling one-year Data & Analytics roadmap, balancing urgent business needs with foundational work. Guide Vahid through clear priorities, design reviews, code review, and reusable modeling patterns.

  • Lead discovery across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Finance to uncover the decision behind a request and translate it into agreed metric definitions, governed semantic layers, and data models that connect the full customer lifecycle.

  • Set the analytical architecture and dbt standards; design, build, test, and document the most critical governed models yourself using SQL and dbt.

  • Own the full-funnel measurement framework—from marketing reach, demand generation, attribution, and customer acquisition cost through lead and pipeline conversion, sales cycle, bookings, and revenue to onboarding, product adoption, expansion, renewal, churn, and customer lifetime value. Keep core recurring-revenue definitions finance-grade and reconciled while showing how upstream activity drives downstream customer outcomes.

  • Own the logic and quality behind executive dashboards and self-service analytics across Power BI, Metabase, and AI-enabled interfaces. Present the results to senior leaders, explain every assumption, and respond constructively to challenge.

  • Partner closely with Vahid on warehouse and pipeline requirements, resolve conflicting numbers at the source, and raise the technical quality of the team. Apply AI where it improves development speed or data access, while using sound judgment around privacy, governance, validation, and trust.

A Typical Week

This is a hands-on lead role. The exact balance will shift with business priorities, but you should expect roughly half your time to remain close to the data—building, reviewing, and investigating—and the rest to be split across discovery, functional leadership, and decision support.

  • Design or improve a dbt model that connects data across HubSpot, our LMS, billing, or other source systems; write the SQL, tests, documentation, and metric logic needed to put it into production.

  • Run discovery sessions with leaders in Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Product, or Finance to clarify the decision they need to make, challenge the requested metric, and agree on the definition.

  • Work side by side with Vahid on source-data requirements, architecture choices, and implementation; review code and unblock delivery without handing off all of the technical work.

  • Investigate a commercial or customer-lifecycle question, improve an executive or functional dashboard, and present the conclusion—including assumptions and limitations—to the relevant leadership team.

  • Reprioritize the Data & Analytics roadmap, resolve competing requests, and invest in the semantic layer, governance, and reusable modeling foundations that reduce future ad hoc work.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first three months, you have established a clear operating model with Vahid, mapped ownership of the most important metrics, agreed the Data & Analytics roadmap, and resolved at least one material conflicting-number problem.

Within six months, AIHR has a governed customer-lifecycle domain in dbt and an executive view connecting acquisition and pipeline to revenue, retention, and product usage, and has launched the first MVP of our agentic analytics platform to drive self-serve adoption. The underlying definitions are documented, reconciled where relevant, and trusted across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Finance.

Within twelve months, two or three priority business domains are governed end to end, leadership can trace performance from acquisition through lifetime value using consistent numbers, self-service adoption is growing, and Vahid can independently implement the modeling patterns and quality standards you established.

Throughout, you remain hands-on in SQL, dbt, Snowflake, and analytics while setting direction, coaching through the work, and earning leadership's trust in both the numbers and the roadmap.

We offer

  • A high-impact role as the functional lead of a small Data & Analytics team, with end-to-end ownership of the semantic layer behind company-wide decisions.

  • Competitive, benchmarked compensation.

  • Substantial autonomy to shape your day-to-day work, with regular growth conversations and support for your career goals.

  • Flexible working hours and work-from-home arrangements after onboarding.

  • 26 paid holidays per year, plus one extra day for each of your first five years at AIHR.

  • The option to exchange any two public holidays for two days of your choice.

  • A work-from-anywhere policy that lets you work abroad for up to 20 days per calendar year.

  • A pension plan, four Trust Days for ad hoc recovery, and access to the OpenUp mental health platform.

  • A personal development budget, training opportunities, and the books you need to keep learning.

  • All public-transport expenses covered through an NS Business Card, plus a MacBook and the equipment you need.

  • A beautiful office opposite Rotterdam Central Station, a satellite office in Amsterdam, daily chef-prepared lunch, regular drinks, team activities, and free access to the office gym.

Get a taste of working at AIHR in our AIHR Benefits Guide.

Apply for the Job

Are you excited to become our Lead Analytics Engineer? We would love to hear from you. We are aiming for a start date in December 2026 or January 2027.

P.S. If this role excites you but you do not meet every point, we still encourage you to apply. We care about the evidence behind your experience and your potential to grow—not a perfect checklist.


Who you are

You are a hands-on technical leader: commercially sharp, calm under challenge, and confident enough to defend your numbers in any room. You also have the patience to build data foundations properly and raise the quality of the work around you.

  • You bring 5+ years of experience across analytics engineering, BI, data engineering, or business-facing analytics roles, including substantial recent hands-on analytics engineering and evidence of leading work beyond your own delivery.

  • You have a proven track record of building semantic layers or governed dimensional models end-to-end—from business discovery and metric definition to production models and adoption—not only dashboards.

  • You have expert SQL and data modeling skills, strong production experience with dbt, and hands-on experience with Snowflake or a comparable warehouse, along with a BI tool such as Power BI, Looker, Omni, or Metabase.

  • You bring strong financial acumen, but your analytical experience extends across the full customer lifecycle. You can connect marketing acquisition and attribution, sales pipeline and conversion, revenue and unit economics, customer retention and expansion, and product adoption into one coherent model. You understand how bookings, billings, recognized revenue, cash, ARR, and NRR differ without treating financial reporting as the whole analytical problem.

  • You have worked in a B2B SaaS, subscription, fintech, or marketplace business and have modeled several stages of the funnel spanning marketing or growth, sales, customer success and retention, and product usage—rather than specializing in only one function.

  • You explain complex logic in plain language, push back constructively on senior stakeholders, and build trust without becoming defensive—even when you discover that your own number or assumption needs to change.

  • You take pride in driving the analytical roadmap and architectural vision, leading technical work through architecture and code review, and mentoring experienced colleagues without relying on formal authority. You want the majority of your role to remain hands-on.

  • You balance pragmatic execution with rigorous analysis, adapting precision levels to fit business needs and operational constraints.

  • You are used to leveraging a broad range of AI tools to boost your productivity and know how to configure them to produce output that lives up to our quality standards and best practices

Nice to Have

Being a fast-growing company, working at AIHR means taking on a lot of responsibility and getting countless opportunities to develop yourself in new areas and potential to craft your own role.


Role and Responsibilities

As our Senior Sales Operations Manager, your job is to make it easier for Sales to do great work. This is a hands-on role with a broad view of the commercial journey. You’ll work on how Sales operates, support leadership with better insight, and own processes such as the Deal Desk, vendor registration, invoicing, collections, and order-to-cash.

We see those responsibilities as connected. Being close to the day-to-day work gives you the context to see where time is being lost, where a process no longer works, and where the same problem keeps coming back. We want someone who is comfortable doing the work themselves, but who does not simply accept unnecessary manual work because “that’s how we do it.”

This role is a combination of keeping things moving today and making sure they work better tomorrow.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Improving how Sales works. You use data, feedback, and your understanding of the day-to-day work to identify where things can be better. That could mean redesigning a workflow, improving reporting, clarifying ownership, creating a better operating rhythm, or removing manual steps that no longer add value.

  • Helping Sales leadership improve performance. You look beyond individual requests and help spot patterns across the Sales organization. Where are deals slowing down? What does the data tell us about why? Are we missing information in HubSpot that would help Sales, Marketing, or leadership make better decisions? You turn those observations into practical recommendations and are comfortable challenging existing ways of working when the data points somewhere else.

  • Owning and improving the Deal Desk. When a deal needs something outside the standard process, you help move it forward. This can include approvals, documentation, commercial questions, vendor or supplier registration, procurement portals, questionnaires, and coordination across internal and external stakeholders. You take care of the immediate need, while also looking for patterns that could make the next request simpler.

  • Owning order-to-cash and collections. You take responsibility for turning booked revenue into collected cash. Collections is a meaningful and hands-on part of the role: monitoring outstanding invoices, following up with customers, picking up the phone when that is the best way to resolve an issue, and working with Sales, Finance, procurement teams, and other stakeholders to clear payment blockers. You also look at the process behind the work — reducing overdue balances, improving follow-up, and finding ways to make order-to-cash more effective over time.

  • Working AI-first. You actively use AI and automation where they can make the work more efficient or improve the quality of the outcome. That might mean analyzing patterns in Sales data, speeding up vendor registration, improving a recurring workflow, or removing repetitive administrative work. Being a fast-growing company, working at AIHR means taking on a lot of responsibility. For a senior hire, that means real ownership: the room to shape a commercial channel, direct access to leadership, and the potential to craft your own role as the program grows.

Role and Responsibilities

As Senior Partnership Manager, you come in with the ambition to triple the AIHR partnership program. Today that program is a global portfolio of 130+ commercial partners driving primarily single-seat e-commerce sales, plus a reseller channel that brings in B2B business. Both work, and both have far more potential than we currently capture. Your job is to optimize what we have, evolve it into a set of structured commercial partner programs, and work out which new channels deserve investment.

This is a quota-carrying role with a build mandate. You manage a running book of business with our existing commercial partners and stay their main point of contact. On top of that, you design and launch larger partner programs with resellers, HR consultancies, system integrators, and universities. We have a strong belief that these partners, HR implementation consultants in particular, are well placed to position our courses with their clients, and that this can become a major revenue stream for AIHR.

Your work is built from three connected workstreams:

  • Grow the existing partner channel: run the existing book, grow partner revenue, and identify the commercial opportunities that drive meaningful additional business.

  • Build the extended partner programs: restructure the reseller program so it generates more predictable, repeatable B2B revenue, and extend it to consultancies, system integrators, and universities.

  • Define the tech partnership go-to-market: research which commercial models fit AIHR, propose the strategy, then test, validate, and build out what works.

You’ll report to the Team Lead for Channel & Strategic Partnerships, work closely with Marketing, Sales, and Product to get your partners what they need, and act as the partnership network’s advocate across the wider commercial team. You will regularly present proposals and results to AIHR leadership.

On a typical day

On a typical Monday morning, you start with your pipeline. Your existing partner book is quick to review: a few conversations need a nudge, two QBRs are coming up. The larger partnerships take more thought. Other companies in our industry have built significant revenue through resellers, consultancies, and universities, but these deals have a longer sales cycle, so you always keep several opportunities moving at the same time. Today that means a value-added reseller in the middle of a negotiation, a prospective university that wants to add AIHR’s courses to its 2027 academic year, and a consultancy that signed last month and now needs to get moving.

After lunch you speak with the managing partner of a German niche consultancy that does a lot of HR implementation work. Her clients keep running into the same problem: the new system goes live, and the HR team lacks the skills to get the most out of it. You talk through how capability building could become part of her offering, with AIHR as the partner behind it. She is interested, and you agree to work out a commercial proposal together. Next you work on an enablement session for consultants, covering what they need to know about our courses, how they bring AIHR into a client conversation, what a first joint win could look like, and you brief Marketing on the materials their consultants will need.

The next morning is for outreach. You build a sourcing list of potential partners in a segment you want to open up, and you contact them yourself. AIHR has a very good name in the HR industry, and that usually helps open doors. Later that week you run a QBR with one of your strongest commercial partners. You review their numbers together, agree on two concrete actions, and set a date to check back in. You identify where there is room to grow the relationship and push for more where performance has stalled. You also notice that a large part of their customer base works in corporate HR teams, so you bring in a colleague from Sales to explore a B2B opportunity through the same relationship.

On Thursday you are back with the value-added reseller. They want to bundle our courses with their own services. It is a model we haven’t proven yet. There is no standard agreement to pull off the shelf, so you work with our Sales Engineer to design the deal while you negotiate it: what they sell, how they are rewarded, how revenue is generated, and what would tell you both it is working. You treat it as a pilot and agree on a first version you can learn from. Some of these experiments will not work out. The ones that do become the programs you build the channel on, and you will be the person who figured them out.

You close out the week updating your forecast and walking your manager through where the existing book, pipeline, and new programs stand. Friday afternoon wraps with a quick team catch-up and, if you're in the Rotterdam office, our regular Friday drinks.

Your Target

This is a quota-carrying role. Your number is built from the revenue of the partner book you run and the new partner programs you launch. In your first year, that means growing revenue across the existing partner portfolio, a restructured reseller program, the first signed partners among consultancies, system integrators, and universities, and a tech partnership go-to-market strategy that has been proposed, tested, and started generating commercial opportunities.

Zo kun je bijvoorbeeld bedrijven helpen met het inzichtelijk maken van hun data of meedenken over hoe ze veiliger met hun data om kunnen gaan. Je helpt onze klanten vooruit door ze mee te nemen in nieuwe technologieën en te laten zien waar bijvoorbeeld AI daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegt. Op deze manier kun je zowel kleine, maar ook grote en veeleisende bedrijven helpen met oplossingen die kritisch zijn voor hun bedrijfsvoering.  

Tenslotte zorgen wij er samen voor dat jij continu blijft groeien en op de hoogte bent van de nieuwste ontwikkelingen. 

 

Wat ga je doen?  

Als Data Engineer bij PuurData ben je meer dan een technicus. Je bent een consultant die klanten helpt om meer waarde uit hun data te halen. PuurData werkt met platformen zoals Elastic en AWS, en bedient klanten op het gebied van zoektechnologie, observability, security en AI. Jij bent degene die die oplossingen tot leven brengt.

Je start bij de klant. Je inventariseert de vraag: wat willen ze met hun data? Gaat het om betere zoekfunctionaliteit, real-time inzicht in systemen, of security en threat detection? Vervolgens ga je samen met de klant naar de juiste oplossing toe. Je vertaalt de behoefte naar een concrete aanpak en implementeert die van A tot Z: van het inrichten van de datastroom tot het opleveren van dashboards en inzichten.

Geen dag is hetzelfde. De use cases lopen uiteen van zoekoplossingen en business process monitoring tot SIEM-implementaties en data engineering-pipelines. Dat geeft je veel vrijheid in de invulling van je werk.

Continu leren is geen optie, maar de norm
Technologie staat niet stil, en jij ook niet. Bij PuurData is training verplicht. Je blijft op de hoogte van de laatste ontwikkelingen, denk aan Elastic, AI-integraties en nieuwe dataplatformen, en past die kennis direct toe in klantprojecten.

Je bent een ondernemende professional die weinig sturing nodig heeft. Je kunt technische keuzes helder onderbouwen en klanten daarin meenemen, ook als het complex is. Daarin mag je best een tikkeltje eigenwijs zijn.

Geen probleem. Als je leergierig bent en en affiniteit hebt met data, komen we graag met je in contact.

  • Technical and economic feasibility. Preparing structured assessments and reports on technical feasibility, process requirements, raw materials, costs and potential economic viability.

  • Test programme development. Supporting the design of experimental programmes, including formulation matrices, variables, testing methods and evaluation criteria.

  • Data analysis. Processing and evaluating experimental data to identify trends, correlations, performance drivers and development priorities.

  • Programming, data analysis and AI-assisted workflows. Using Python and modern AI-assisted development tools, including AI agents, to clean, structure, analyse and visualize technical data; automate repetitive R&D tasks; support technical research; and build internal analytical workflows. A key part of the role is learning to use these tools effectively and responsibly, with proper validation, documentation and control of the resulting work.

  • Technical standards and regulations. Researching and analysing standards, specifications and regulatory requirements relevant to products under development and their potential applications.

Requirements

title: Financial Controller (w/m/d)
description:
Tangany mit Sitz in München ist ein innovatives Technologieunternehmen mit einer marktführenden B2B-Lösung für die Verwahrung digitaler Vermögenswerte (z. B. Kryptowährungen, Stablecoins und anderen tokenisierten Vermögenswerten) in Blockchain-Netzwerken. Unsere Lösung wird bereits von mehr als 50 institutionellen Kunden eingesetzt. Als lizenziertes Finanzinstitut wird die Tangany GmbH von der BaFin reguliert.

Für unser anhaltendes Wachstum suchen wir einen Financial Controller (w/m/d) zur Verstärkung unseres Teams.

Deine Rolle

Du verantwortest das Controlling und die Finanzsteuerung und berichtest an das Management Board.

Das Team ist klein. Deine Expertise und dein Beitrag wirken sich unmittelbar aus: Du arbeitest mit unserer Accountant und unserer Steuerkanzlei z.B. an Themen wie Finanzbuchhaltung, Lohn und Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung; die formale Verantwortung für das Rechnungswesen liegt bei der Geschäftsleitung, Zahlungen geben wir im Vier-Augen-Prinzip frei. In diesem Rahmen bist du die Person, die weiß, wo die Zahlen stehen, warum sie dort stehen und wie sich Ergebnis, Kosten, Liquidität und Eigenmittel entwickeln werden.

Der Kern der Rolle hat zwei Seiten: die regulatorische Pflicht und eine Steuerung, mit der wir jede Finanzfrage jederzeit in wenigen Minuten beantworten können. Business Cases und Investor Reporting kommen dazu und wachsen mit dir.

Heute arbeiten wir vor allem mit DATEV Unternehmen Online und Tableau. Die Steuerung darauf baust du zu großen Teilen neu auf, gern AI-gestützt: Unser AI-Dev-Team setzt mit dir Live-Reporting, Abstimmungen und ein Finanz-Cockpit um.

Aufgaben

  • Den Jahresabschluss nach HGB und RechKredV erstellen, ergänzt um die RechZahlV-Posten für unser Zahlungsgeschäft, und die Prüfung gemeinsam mit unserer Steuerkanzlei und Abschlussprüfer durchführen.

  • Das aufsichtsrechtliche Meldewesen führen und Finanzinformationen nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben unter Begleitung des Compliance-Teams bereitstellen.

  • Regulatorische Planzahlen, etwa die Eigenmittelanforderung, aus der Bilanzplanung ableiten und in Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsleitung laufend überwachen.

  • Cashflow- und Runway-Planung führen und Finanzierungsbedarf früh sichtbar machen.

  • Liquiditäts- und Kontrahentenrisiken in das unternehmensweite Risikocontrolling einbringen und laufend überwachen.

  • Business Cases und Rentabilitätsrechnungen erstellen und Investor-Updates vorbereiten.

  • Eine Kostenstellenstruktur aufbauen, Budgets je Kostenstelle mit den Verantwortlichen festlegen, Kosten, Budgets und KPIs laufend überwachen sowie Live-Reporting und Ad-hoc-Auswertungen für Geschäftsleitung und Budgetverantwortliche bereitstellen und Plan-Ist-Abweichungen analysieren.

  • Aus der Praxiserfahrung heraus Input liefern, um Finanzprozesse, Tools und das interne Kontrollsystem gemeinsam mit unserem AI-Dev-Team auszubauen.

Wen wir suchen

  • Du bist Controller:in (idealerweise aus einem regulierten Institut) und hast Jahresabschluss und Meldewesen selbst verantwortet.

  • Abweichungen erkennst du früh: Wenn sich Eigenmittel, Liquidität oder Kosten in die falsche Richtung bewegen, liegt deine Analyse mit Optionen auf dem Tisch, solange noch Zeit zum Handeln ist.

  • Deine Forecasts halten auch Monate später, und wo sie abweichen, kannst du erklären, warum.

  • Meldefristen und Prüfungsanforderungen baust du so in die Abläufe ein, dass vor dem Stichtag keine Ad-hoc Aktion nötig ist.

  • Prüfer und Risikocontrolling nehmen deine Zahlen als Ausgangspunkt.

  • Stellt die Geschäftsleitung eine Finanzfrage, kannst du schnell und problemlos Antworten geben, weil deine Daten und Auswertungen genau dafür gebaut sind.

  • Du entscheidest auch mit unvollständigen Informationen, sagst klar, wenn etwas nicht geht, und stellst einen Prozess um, sobald er nicht mehr passt.

Qualifikation

Must-Haves

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium oder Ausbildung in Finanzen, Controlling oder einem verwandten Feld.

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung im Controlling oder Rechnungswesen, idealerweise in einem regulierten Institut (nach KWG, ZAG oder MiCAR) oder in der Prüfung entsprechender Institute.

  • Eigenständig erstellte Jahresabschlüsse nach HGB, sowie Erfahrung mit Liquiditäts- und Kontrahentenrisiken sowie Risikotragfähigkeit.

  • Aufbau von Kostenstellenrechnung und Management-Reporting, sicherer Umgang mit DATEV, Excel und Google Sheets inklusive Finanzmodellen und deren Visualisierung, idealerweise mit einem BI-Tool wie Tableau.

  • Offenheit: Reporting mit AI-Werkzeugen neu aufsetzen.

  • Fließend Deutsch und Englisch (C1 oder höher).

Nice-to-Haves

  • Erfahrung mit MiCAR, etwa der Eigenmittelberechnung.

  • FP&A, Business Cases oder Investor-Reporting in einem wachsenden Unternehmen.

  • Erfahrung im aufsichtsrechtlichen Meldewesen nach KWG oder ZAG.

  • Interesse an Krypto und Tokenisierung.

Benefits

Flexibilität & Work-Life-Balance:

  • 30 Tage Urlaub, dazu jeweils ein halber Tag frei an Heiligabend und Silvester, und bei Bedarf zusätzlicher unbezahlter Urlaub, um die Akkus wieder aufzuladen.

  • Zusätzlicher bezahlter Urlaub für frischgebackene Eltern.

Students explore the topic through research, interviews and real enterprise cases (month 1), classify goals, talent profiles and success patterns (month 2), and build strategy blueprints, a final report and a pitch to Mediacharge leadership (month 3). title: Founding Recruiter (m/f/x)
description:
01 · Why this role exists

Invest in Values. Produce in Freedom. Boost Europe.

Behind every megawatt hour our clients save, there are people who make it happen. RIZM helps Europe's largest industrial companies – together around 2% of Europe's total energy demand – make their energy decisions with AI. Our agent RIZMO works as a digital colleague. But the most important colleagues are the ones we haven't found yet.

That's your job. We're about 15 people today and growing fast. There is no recruiting playbook yet, no big HR department and no "that's how we've always done it". You'll write the playbook. Not as application admin, but as the person who shapes who RIZM becomes.

02 · Hi, we're Diana and Josh – we'll be working together

I'm Diana, 20, I study civil engineering in Münster and I currently run recruiting at RIZM on my own, 20 hours a week. That's not enough for what's ahead of us, which is why we're looking for you. We'll build this together, side by side in our Münster office. Josh, our co-founder & CBO, comes from statistics and risk management and will be your sparring partner whenever you need one – for tricky candidates, for offers and for figuring out who we need next. Got questions before you apply? Just message me on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/diana-pashaian-1637133b2/

03 · What you'll do

  • Build the team of tomorrow: Design our recruiting from scratch – roles, workflows, tools – and later bring more recruiters and sourcers on board yourself.

  • Find the right people: Track down engineers, energy experts and product people via LinkedIn, Juicebox, universities, communities and your own network.

  • Win people over: Lead first conversations, tell our story convincingly and make sure every candidate feels well looked after – even when it's a no.

  • Make it smart: Automate sequences, screening and reporting with AI instead of maintaining spreadsheets.

  • Steer by numbers: Always know where the funnel gets stuck – and turn the right dials.

  • Get us seen: Shape how RIZM is perceived as an employer – careers page, job ads, events, university partnerships.

04 · What you bring

  • Experience: You've worked in recruiting or talent acquisition, ideally in startups or tech, and you know how to approach technical profiles.

  • People sense: You spot potential even when it's not on the CV, and you talk to engineers as equals.

  • Tech affinity: You try out new tools, build your own workflows and enjoy making things faster.

  • Builder drive: You don't want to step into ready-made structures – you want to create them, independently, reliably and fast.

  • Background: A degree in psychology, business, HR, social sciences or similar – or a path that prepared you just as well.

  • Languages: Fluent German and English, written and spoken.

05 · What you get

  • Performance counts: Uncapped variable pay plus equity – good work is visible here and rewarded directly.

  • Real ownership: You're the first recruiter. What you build stays.

  • A network that moves you forward: Sparring, mentoring and learning with the networks of our investors Point 9 and Earlybird.

  • Once a year, we get out: A team workation with everyone, including conversations with inspiring guests like Robert Habeck, Kitty Mayo or James Vincent.

  • Stay fit: Urban Sports Club membership.

  • Münster office: You sit right next to our engineering team – the people you'll hire most – and you hear first-hand what makes a great engineer at RIZM. Recruiting thrives on short distances – the best ideas come up at the same table.

06 · How to apply

You don't need to write a classic cover letter. We don't think it tells us much about a person anymore.

Instead, picture this: a few years from now, RIZM welcomes its 100th team member. There's a celebration in the Münster office. One of the first people you ever hired stands up to say a few words.

- What's the one thing you hope they say about you?

- And what have you done so far that makes you believe they would?

A few honest sentences are enough.

Der ultimative TYPO3-Check

  • … sofort merkst, wenn dir die KI eine TypoScript-Lösung aus dem Jahr 2014 andreht. Und sie trotzdem jeden Tag nutzt, weil sie dich schneller macht.

  • … und dein Gewissen dir verbietet, freitags um 16 Uhr ein Major-Update auf Production zu schieben. Auch nicht „nur schnell“.

… dann gilt für uns nur noch eins: composer require netfed/du

title: (Senior) Strategic Partner Manager   (f/m/d)
description:
At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions.

Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next.

London, UK

Moss is building its strategic partnerships function from scratch, and this is one of the first two hires shaping it. You'll take target platforms from zero relationship to live, revenue-generating integration, owning the sourcing, business case, and delivery for each one.

This is a build phase: you'll define your own playbook rather than follow one. You'll report to the Senior Director Partnerships and work closely with Product and Engineering on integration scope, and with the Channel team where partnerships overlap with existing ERP integrators.

Your responsibilities

  • Source and build strategic partnerships from scratch, identifying platforms that fit Moss's customer base and growth priorities

  • Navigate complex partner organisations to reach the right decision makers, from founders and C-level contacts at smaller platforms to Heads of Partnerships at larger ones

  • Build the commercial and technical case for each partnership and secure buy-in from both Moss leadership and the partner's stakeholders

  • Own each partnership end-to-end, from an initial referral or lightweight integration through to a live, revenue-generating relationship

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to scope integration requirements and manage delivery against Moss's API and roadmap

  • Collaborate with the Channel team where accounting-platform integrators already exist, to avoid overlap and align on commercialisation

  • Define and adjust your own playbook, prioritising partners by revenue potential and strategic fit as the market picture sharpens

About you

  • 5+ years in business development or partnerships within B2B SaaS, fintech, cloud, or payments

  • At least 2 years specifically in strategic partnerships or integration-led partner roles, having built relationships from scratch rather than managed an existing book

  • Working knowledge of APIs and how software platforms integrate with external partner systems

In addition, here are the skills and attributes we are looking for:

  • Thrives with full ownership of a plan and pipeline, without needing day-to-day direction

  • Brings structure to ambiguous, still-being-built processes and partnerships

  • Communicates progress, blockers, and trade-offs clearly across product, engineering, and leadership

  • Balances ambition with realism, adjusting timelines to partner readiness and internal constraints without losing momentum

About Moss

Moss is the Finance AI platform for Europe's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work.

Founded in Berlin and used by more than 10,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, n8n and Auto1, Moss has raised €220+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. Data protection is central to what we do.   • We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake.

The role

As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing.

The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver.

There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business.

You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator.

  • Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows.   • AI and automated decisioning.   • AI and automation. A real interest in, and working understanding of, how data protection law applies to AI and automated decision-making. Enough technical fluency to see where a manual process could be automated, set out what is needed, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

 

Why we're hiring

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

 

About the role

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

  • Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

  • Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

  • Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

  • Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

  • Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

  • Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

 

What this role isn't

  • An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

  • A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

  • A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

  • A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

  • A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

 

What success looks like

In your first 90 days:

  • The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

  • Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

  • You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

  • Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

  • At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

  • We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

  • You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

  • The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

  • Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

  • Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

 

About you

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

  • You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

  • You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

  • You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

  • You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

  • You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

 

How you will grow

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

 

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

  • 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

  • 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

  • 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

  • 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

  • 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

 

The environment

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

title: wo-stage economie: Nowcasting Model voor BBP
description:
wo-praktijkstage,

start in overleg

Krijg jij energie van het bouwen van slimme datamodellen die economische groei voorspellen nog voordat alle cijfers binnen zijn? Duik jij graag in data, ontdek je nieuwe databronnen en wil je met jouw analyses échte impact maken op officiële bbp-ramingen?
Dan is deze stage in nowcasting en econometrie precies wat je zoekt.

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Bij het ramen van de kwartaalcijfers van het bbp (economische groei) gebruiken we voor een aantal bedrijfstakken momenteel een relatief eenvoudige methode: de ontwikkeling van het aantal banen dient als benadering voor de economische activiteit. Dit gebeurt omdat directe en tijdige broninformatie ontbreekt. Een belangrijk gevolg hiervan is dat we de eerste ramingen later vaak moeten bijstellen wanneer er meer volledige data beschikbaar komt bij de definitieve raming (ongeveer anderhalf jaar later).

Het is aan jou om deze methodiek te verbeteren.

Je gaat een geavanceerder model ontwikkelen waarmee we de economische activiteit van deze bedrijfstakken kort na afloop van de verslagperiode nauwkeuriger kunnen inschatten. Dit wordt ook wel “nowcasting” genoemd. Het doel is om dichter bij de uiteindelijke realisatie te zitten en daarmee het aantal en de omvang van latere bijstellingen te verkleinen.

Een belangrijk onderdeel van jouw opdracht is om te onderzoeken welke databronnen tijdig beschikbaar zijn en we kunnen gebruiken als input voor dit model. Vervolgens ga je met behulp van historische data eerdere verslagperiodes simuleren. Zo kun je analyseren of jouw voorgestelde methode daadwerkelijk beter presteert dan de huidige aanpak, bijvoorbeeld door te kijken naar kleinere bijstellingen.

Tot slot ontwikkel je een werkende productiestraat in R, zodat de nieuwe methode praktisch toepasbaar wordt binnen het ramingproces.

bij CBS Den Haag

De nationale rekeningen vormen de officiële overzichtsstatistiek van de nationale economie. Het nationaal inkomen, de economische groei, het overheidstekort en het beschikbaar inkomen van huishoudens zijn enkele belangrijke macro-economische indicatoren die aan de hand van de nationale rekeningen worden vastgesteld.

Binnen ons team heerst een open, betrokken en collegiale sfeer.

Dit breng jij mee

  • Je volgt een economische wo-opleiding met een duidelijke kwantitatieve component.

  • Je werkt nauwkeurig en gestructureerd, zowel met data als met code en documentatie.

  • Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor je eigen werk: je plant, organiseert en bewaakt je voortgang gedurende de stage.

Dit is jouw uitdaging

Het CBS trekt steekproeven onder de Nederlandse bevolking om diverse statistieken te maken. Hierbij is sprake van selectieve non-respons. Om voor deze non-respons te corrigeren, voeren we een zogenaamde weging uit, waarbij personen een gewicht krijgen op basis van hun onder- of oververtegenwoordiging in de respons. Personen met achtergrondkenmerken die ondervertegenwoordigd zijn in de respons, krijgen dan een groter gewicht dan personen met achtergrondkenmerken die oververtegenwoordigd zijn. Zie bijvoorbeeld [1] voor algemene informatie over wegen.

Bij het uitvoeren van een weging zijn er diverse zaken om rekening mee te houden. Zo kan niet voor alle achtergrondkenmerken worden gecorrigeerd voor scheefheid, omdat de gewichten dan te extreem zouden worden. Daarnaast is het vaak verstandig om überhaupt niet voor te veel achtergrondkenmerken te corrigeren, omdat dit een negatieve invloed heeft op de marges van de schattingen voor de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek. Ook is er een relatie met de doelvariabelen in het onderzoek: op het moment dat er een samenhang is tussen een achtergrondkenmerk en de doelvariabelen van een onderzoek, is het wenselijk om wél voor dat achtergrondkenmerk te corrigeren als dat kenmerk scheef in de respons zit. Het is daarom vaak verstandig om toch zo veel mogelijk te corrigeren voor scheefheid in achtergrondkenmerken.

Het CBS heeft een reguliere werkwijze voor het opstellen en uitvoeren van wegingen voor reguliere onderzoeken. Een optie die nog niet wordt gebruikt, maar wel interessant lijkt, is het uitvoeren van een zogenaamde voorweging. Hierbij wordt de weging min of meer in twee stappen uitgevoerd, waardoor er mogelijk voor meer en/of andere achtergrondkenmerken gecorrigeerd kan worden. Wellicht is het mogelijk om eerst een correctie uit te voeren voor non-respons en vervolgens een verdere weging uit te voeren die meer focust op de doelvariabelen van het onderzoek en de achtergrondkenmerken die daarmee correleren. Dit soort vragen speelt zowel bij de reguliere steekproeven die bij het CBS worden uitgevoerd als bij potentiële nieuwe toepassingen. In deze stage ga je aan de slag om verschillende opties voor de weging te analyseren, te kijken naar de verschillen tussen deze opties en te bepalen welke keuze de voorkeur heeft.

Afhankelijk van de resultaten zouden weegmethoden aangepast kunnen worden, met directe impact op de statistieken van het CBS.
