  • You are autonomous on day-to-day People on-call requests;

  • You have mapped our current M&A and country-opening practices and shared a first list of gaps and quick wins;

  • You have contributed to the People workstream of at least one live deal or country opening (due diligence, contract transfer or integration);

  • You have contributed to our reusable playbook (e.g. HR due diligence checklist);

  • You have shadowed and been reverse-shadowed on individual situation management.

By 5 months:

  • Depending on the ongoing projects, you own the People workstream of a deal end to end, from due diligence to integration, with the crew as a sounding board;

  • You have run, or co-run, one talent density assessment and the parting ways cases that came with it;

  • You handle cross-border individual situations without supervision;

  • Your playbooks are used by the crew and by Legal / Finance on new deals;

  • Leads and crew members come to you as the go-to expert on these topics.

 

Is this what you are looking for?

You may be a great fit for this role if:

  • You have around 5 years of experience focused on HR M&A and integration topics, for example in a reputable HR advisory firm or in an HR team that focuses on these topics.

  • You have worked on acquisitions in the Tech industry, not only on very large corporate groups, and you know the method is not the same.

  • You master HR due diligence and the transfer of employment contracts.

  • You have worked on post-merger integration, including talent density and parting ways, not only on the pre-signing side.

  • You have international exposure: you have worked on deals or entities outside France.

  • You are fluent in English, written and spoken (all of our internal processes, documentation and communications are in English).

  • You are adaptable and creative: you adjust your method to each type of company and deal instead of copy-pasting one process.

  • You are very organised: you run several confidential workstreams in parallel without dropping balls.

  • You are a strong communicator, with very different audiences (founders, acquired employees, leads, lawyers), in writing and orally.

  • You are strong technically and can teach us things.

  • You show judgement and discretion with confidential information and sensitive human situations.

Nice-to-have

We are not looking for all of the below. Any one of these can be a strong signal.

  • You have a legal background, ideally in employment law.

  • You have worked in or with a Tech scale-up that made several acquisitions.

  • You have opened entities or set-up employers of record in new countries.

  • You speak another language relevant to our expansion (e.g. Spanish, Portuguese; Arabic).

  • You are AI-enthusiastic and actively use tools to multiply your impact.

Level range

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range.

title: Elektronik-Ingenieur
description:
About pplwise
pplwise is a recruiting consultancy for fast-growing technology companies across Europe. Through Recruiting as a Service and Executive Search, we fill key roles for our clients, from start-ups to publicly listed companies. We are filling this position for our client Filics.

About our client: Filics
Filics is reinventing intralogistics with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that change how material moves. Its double-runner system makes Filics the first and only AMR that can drive through load carriers such as Euro pallets. This breaks with forklift logic and sets a new standard for efficiency. Filics is a small, hands-on team that solves hard problems with engineering excellence. Leadership goes to those who take initiative and consistently deliver. As Senior Electrical Engineer (m/f/d) at Filics, you will design the electronics at the core of the next generation of robots.

About the role
This is an on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to engineering and assembly.

Filics doesn’t just use off-the-shelf components. It builds its own custom IP. The robots run on advanced boards that cover a wide range of electrical engineering. On one end is high power, such as battery and motor controllers. On the other end are high-speed interfaces like PCIe, USB and MIPI CSI. The real challenge is making all these subsystems work together as one system. Many of these problems have no textbook solution. Solving them takes solid experience, a deep understanding of the physics and a creative mind.

The EE team is small, and the robot is far from finished. You’ll own your boards end to end: requirements, system design, schematic, layout, design review, sourcing, manufacturing, testing and validation. You’ll keep owning them for as long as they’re in production. You’ll work closely with Embedded Software, Mechanical Engineering, Software and the Production team. As Filics moves from prototypes to series production, your designs need to work reliably at scale, not just in the lab.

What you’ll do

  • Take full ownership of a complex PCB project and get it running in as few revisions as possible

  • Design high-power and high-speed circuits and make sure they work together at system level

  • Design for EMC, manufacturability and testability, and take boards through EMC testing and certification

  • Bring new technical approaches to the team, for example a new converter architecture that enables higher charging power in a smaller package

  • Introduce useful processes from your experience, such as simulation workflows that validate a layout before it goes to production

  • Help with board bring-up and debugging together with Embedded Software, and support Production with clear documentation and training

  • Take over ownership of existing boards so the team shares responsibility

About you

  • Several years designing electronics in an R&D environment at a smaller hardware company driven by innovation (e.g. robotics, e-mobility, aviation, autonomous vehicles, motion control)

  • A proven record of taking PCBs within a larger system from requirements to a validated product

  • Strong skills in schematic design and PCB layout (Altium, KiCad, OrCAD or similar)

  • Hands-on debugging experience with an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, VNA or spectrum analyzer, plus soldering

  • Experience with designs that went through EMC testing or CE certification

  • An innovator’s mindset: you have built something new or significantly improved an existing concept

  • Basic simulation know-how (e.g. LTspice, ANSYS, thermal/EM/tolerance analysis); deeper experience is a strong plus

  • Basic experience with Linux and embedded software

  • You work independently, take ownership and thrive without rigid structures

What Filics offers

  • Real ownership of your designs, from first draft to series production

  • Space to innovate and a wide range of technical challenges, from power electronics to high-speed design

  • A small, high-caliber team with close collaboration across disciplines

  • Fast growth: one year at Filics teaches you what usually takes many years at a large company

  • An on-site/hybrid role in Munich, close to Engineering and Assembly

Sound like you? Apply with your CV.

title: Robot Learning Engineer
description:
Why this role is exciting

Rohlik is the leading Central European e-grocer. More than a million customers buy their groceries from us through Rohlik.cz, Knuspr.de, Kifli.hu, Gurkerl.at and Sezamo.ro, choosing from over 17,000 items, delivered within a couple of hours in 15-minute windows.

We are building the autonomous grocer. Maia, our AI assistant, already talks to customers and builds their orders; agents are moving into our buying and logistics; vision models are learning to watch quality. The next frontier is physical: robots taking over more and more of the work in our fulfilment centres, until fresh food moves from producers to households at a cost nobody else can match.

We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job.

You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them.

What you will own and deliver

  • The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong.

  • Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap.

  • The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows.

  • The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations.

  • Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after.

The scope

This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it.

What we are looking for

  • PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted.

  • You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall.

  • You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists.

  • Dataset instincts. You have trained on data you collected yourself, and you know the failure modes that only show up at training tim..

  • Comfortable as the only ML voice. You make the call, write it down, and revisit it when the pilot data says otherwise.

  • AI is how work gets done here. Our engineers use Claude Code and Devin daily, and we expect you to direct agents for the unglamorous parts — harness code, data plumbing, reproduction scripts — while keeping the quality bar exactly where it was.

  • Particularly relevant. Hand-pose estimation or egocentric video in production; multi-camera rigs and time sync; experience post-training robot-learning models; ROS 2.

What success looks like in 90 days

You have written the capture spec and we set up the first rigs against it. Your pilot gates have numbers, the first hours have passed your harness, and you can tell the people who sign the budget, with data, what the next hundred hours should look like.

Are we a good fit?

Take this role if you would rather own the spec that decides whether a dataset becomes an asset or a write-off than tune someone else's model on someone else's data, if a fulfilment centre at 6 a.m. sounds like a lab to you, and if you want the shortest possible line between your technical judgment and a capital decision. Read our culture code and are we a good fit?.

What we offer

  • The physical-AI side of the autonomous grocer, with the capture spec and the first training runs yours from day one

  • A data asset few teams in the world get to build, in fresh groceries, a domain as hard as manipulation gets

  • Off-the-shelf hardware, a managed cloud estate, and a mandate that has already started

  • Benefits — see what we offer

Are you in?

Instead of a cover letter: pick a published human-video-to-robot-policy pipeline you rate, and tell us where it breaks on a warehouse floor where every hand wears a work glove.

title: Staff Application Security Engineer
description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world, processing 25+ trillion data points annually across thousands of connected devices. The Samsara Application Security team protects this vast footprint end-to-end, spanning cloud services, internal systems, and firmware running on IoT hardware in the field.

As a Staff Application Security Engineer, you'll drive the overarching technical direction for our application security and vulnerability management programs. This is a high-visibility role where you'll influence a broad surface area while retaining the flexibility to dive deep into critical domain focus areas as security priorities evolve.

This is a remote position, open to candidates residing in the UK. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if: 

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, and countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
  • You're energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will: 

  • Lead the ongoing strategy, operation, and continuous improvement of Samsara's vulnerability management program, along with other core application security programs — not just execute against an existing process, but define what the process should be.
  • Own and drive down mean time to remediate (MTTR) across the vulnerability backlog, as SLAs tighten.
  • Build and champion automation and tooling that scale vulnerability detection and response across cloud, firmware/IoT, and corporate systems, rather than relying on manual, one-by-one review.
  • Set technical and architectural direction for the program, translating leadership's strategic priorities into a concrete execution plan for the team.
  • Drive remediation by building trust with engineering teams and providing clear, actionable guidance — partnering with technical program management on reporting rather than owning it directly.
  • Mentor and level up other engineers on secure design and remediation practices, and be a technical voice other teams look to when priorities are unclear.
  • Communicate risk and remediation tradeoffs to engineering leadership in terms they can act on, without owning the relationship end to end.
  • Participate in security incident investigations involving high-profile vulnerabilities, assessing potential impact on Samsara's infrastructure.
  • Be regularly on call to support critical vulnerability response.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 10+ years of relevant experience as a cloud engineer or security engineer, including hands-on vulnerability management across a broad, multi-product enterprise environment  — not a single product or team's slice of it.
  • Proficiency in Go, Python, and JavaScript.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently set technical and architectural direction for a security program, and to drive remediation across a broad, multi-surface environment without direct authority over the teams doing the fixing.
  • Significant experience with modern vulnerability management tooling (e.g., Wiz, Semgrep) and deep familiarity with vulnerability scoring frameworks such as CVSS and EPSS.
  • Strong AWS cloud services background.
  • Deep understanding of Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA).
  • Hands-on use of AI/LLM tooling in your own security workflow — triage, detection logic, remediation drafting — plus credibility speaking to how AI is changing the threat landscape and the tooling available to address it.
  • Location: must be based in central or eastern timezones.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience with C/C++, relevant to firmware and embedded systems.
  • Background at a cloud-native, AI-forward company actively building agentic or AI-driven products.
  • Experience with security automation platforms (e.g., Tines) and serverless frameworks (e.g., AWS Lambda).
  • Experience integrating vulnerability management into modern CI/CD pipelines with a "shift-left" mentality.
  • Experience spanning SaaS, firmware, and corporate IT security programs — not just one product line.
  • Experience managing vulnerabilities within a FedRAMP-certified environment.
  • Experience building, extending, or wiring up AI copilots/agents for security workflows (e.g., automated triage, remediation drafting).

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. title: Operations & Automation Associate
description:
About Nous

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

The role

What Nous does for members can feel simple: helping them understand their bills, save money, and avoid admin. Delivering that reliably at scale is much harder.

You’ll join the Operations team at the heart of the business, working on the difficult real-world problems that sit between our members, our product, external suppliers and the systems that make Nous work.

This is not a traditional customer operations role. You’ll spend time close to our members, understanding their questions, investigating things that have gone wrong and learning in detail how our service works. We think that matters: the best systems are usually built by people who have seen the underlying problems first-hand.

But we don’t want you simply to get faster at doing manual work. We want you to spot the pattern, understand why the problem exists, and help build a better way of doing it.

That might mean redesigning a process, building an automation, using AI to remove repetitive work, querying data to understand what is happening, improving an internal tool, or working with Product and Engineering on a more fundamental fix.

You don't need to arrive knowing all of the tools we use. We care much more about how quickly you learn them.

We’re looking for someone early in their career who is unusually curious, quick to learn and good at figuring things out. You might already have built automations or small products yourself. You might instead have worked in operations, consulting, product, analytics or another demanding environment and found yourself constantly looking for better ways to do things.

Either way, we want someone who gets excited by a problem they don't immediately know how to solve.

You’ll have a lot of support from experienced operators, engineers and product people, but also be given a lot of responsibility unusually early in your career. The aim is for you to quickly become someone who can take an undefined operational problem, understand it properly and build a robust solution.

It’s a rare chance to learn how a fast-growing technology company actually works from the inside while building the systems that allow it to scale.

 

About you

You’re smart, curious, ambitious and unusually high-agency.

You don't need a long list of technical tools on your CV. We care much more about how you think, how quickly you learn and what you do when you encounter something you don't understand.

You’ll probably thrive here if you:

  • Have roughly 1–3 years of experience in a demanding environment such as a startup, operations, consulting, product, analytics or similar

  • Learn unusually quickly and enjoy tackling problems you haven't seen before

  • Are technically curious and actively experiment with AI and new tools to make yourself more effective

  • Have evidence that you like building things, whether that's automations, side projects, spreadsheets, scripts, internal tools, processes or something completely different

  • Are comfortable getting into the detail and tracing a problem until you understand what is really happening

  • Can take something messy and ambiguous and impose structure on it

  • Are naturally empathetic and enjoy understanding what a customer actually needs

  • Communicate clearly and directly

  • Are comfortable working directly with customers and frontline problems, and see that as a source of insight

  • Take ownership rather than waiting to be told exactly what to do

This role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants a steep learning curve, real responsibility and the chance to work as part of a team solving difficult problems.

What you’ll be doing

Let’s get the tricky part out of the way: this role doesn’t fit neatly into a traditional box. It combines tax or audit expertise, product knowledge, client relationships and practical implementation.

As a Legal Engineer in our Paris team, you’ll help tax and audit professionals put AI to work in their day-to-day practice. You’ll work with clients from the first demonstration through pilots, onboarding and wider adoption, understanding what they need and building workflows that hold up in real engagements.

Some of what you’ll be doing:

  • Understand the work. Work with tax partners, audit leaders and their teams to identify where Legora can make a meaningful difference, from tax research and advisory to evidence review and audit documentation.

  • Build and test workflows. Translate client needs into working use cases, check outputs against source material and professional standards, and refine the approach with the people using it.

  • Run demonstrations and training. Lead clear, practical sessions grounded in the client’s own work, adapting your approach for practitioners, partners and innovation teams.

  • Own pilots and rollouts. Agree what success looks like, keep stakeholders and timelines aligned, and help teams move from initial experimentation to regular use.

  • Support commercial conversations. Work alongside Go-to-Market and Customer Success colleagues to demonstrate value, address objections and identify opportunities to expand adoption across teams and service lines.

  • Help improve the product. Bring client needs and product gaps back to Product and Engineering with clear examples and enough evidence to act on.

  • Make good work reusable. Turn successful engagements into templates, guides and playbooks that colleagues and clients can use again.

What you bring

You come from tax, audit, assurance or a closely related advisory practice. You may have trained at a Big Four firm, worked at another professional services firm, or built your experience in an in-house function. Perhaps you’ve already moved into innovation, technology implementation or consulting.

You understand the pressure of client deadlines, the importance of defensible conclusions and how much work sits behind a finished report or piece of advice. You also have ideas about how that work could be done better.

  • Are based in Paris, or willing to relocate, and able to work from the office five days per week.

title: Responsable Réadaptation en Urgence

Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 255 millions d'euros, avec 4794 employés dans le monde.

La Direction des Programmes Internationaux (DPI) de Humanité & Inclusion comprend entre autres 5 Directions Géographiques, 4 Directions Techniques, 1 Direction Atlas Logistique et 1 Direction Urgence.

La Direction Urgence est composée de 15 personnes: une équipe en charge de la veille, de l'alerte et de la préparation aux urgences et une équipe en charge des interventions d'urgence au niveau du siège et sur le terrain. Sous la responsabilité du responsable du pool d'urgence et en étroite coordination avec les Spécialistes en Réadaptation Physique et Fonctionnelle du siège, le responsable Réadaptation Physique et Fonctionnelle d'urgence aura la charge de :

 

Participer au diagnostic initial des opérations de réponse d'urgence, à la suite d’une crise humanitaire ;

Diriger et coordonner :

Piloter le déploiement des activités de réadaptation physique et fonctionnelle lors de l’ouverture de nouveaux programmes d’urgence, en assurant la définition du cadre opérationnel, le management des équipes, la coordination avec les autres secteurs d’intervention et les partenaires, ainsi que le suivi de la qualité, du budget, des résultats et du reporting. Représenter et promouvoir le mandat d’Humanité & Inclusion dans le cadre des réponses d’urgence dans votre domaine d’expertise ;

·        Promouvoir le mandat et son positionnement en coordination avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre ;

·        Contribuer à la mobilisation des acteurs publics et privés pour assurer l’inclusion de la vulnérabilité et du handicap dans leurs programmes et initiatives.

 

Contribuer à la capitalisation institutionnelle et participer au développement et à la mise à jour des méthodologies, procédures, outils et formations d'urgence d’Humanité & Inclusion.

·        Participer aux travaux de formalisation et de capitalisation dans son domaine d'expertise en étroite collaboration avec le responsable de secteur et le spécialiste technique du siège ;

·        Contribuer au développement et/ou à l'optimisation des outils, procédures et ressources utilisés par Humanité & Inclusion pour la réponse aux urgences en étroite collaboration avec le spécialiste technique du siège.

·        Contribuer à l'amélioration des outils et modules de formation dans ses domaines d'expertise ;

·        Participer activement aux ateliers organisés au sein de l'Equipe de Réponse aux Urgences ou par d'autres départements au sein d'Humanité & Inclusion, en relation avec les réponses aux urgences

·        Apporter un support au spécialiste technique du siège sur des sujets spécifiques et transversaux.

Requirements

Vous avez une expérience d’au moins trois ans en réadaptation physique et fonctionnelle en contexte d’urgence et votre situation personnelle actuelle vous permet d’être déployé sous 72 heures ? We build companies from zero, putting capital, our own team, and hands-on operating time behind a founding team before there's a product or even a name. The studio's work spans wherever a market and the data or infrastructure underneath it are broken enough to justify building the fix from scratch.

About The General Data Corporation

General Data is the infrastructure for licensing proprietary data: The platform runs the whole deal from request to delivery, with privacy checks, rights evidence and contracts built in. The vision is to become the system of record between AI and the world’s private data, the data that has never been published but that the next generation of AI depends on. On one side are enterprises, AI labs and robotics teams that need real-world data, and on the other are companies whose operations generate it. General Data is the data infrastructure for the modern economy, connecting every party so that data can be licensed safely, transparently and at scale.

Why this is a unique opportunity

AI has absorbed the public internet, and its next gains will come from private, real-world data, yet today these deals still run on email, WhatsApp and brokers, with no visibility into what was checked, who holds the rights, or whether personal data was removed. Labs are already paying for this data, and regulation like GDPR and the EU Data Act makes a trusted, verifiable layer a necessity.

General Data is VC-backed and looking for its technical co-founder. Together with Founder & CEO Louai Allani, you will own the product and architecture, shape the company’s direction as an equal partner and build the team from the ground up.

About the role

  • Supplier intake: Build connectors for where companies actually keep their data: Databases, document stores, ticketing systems, machine logs, and sensor and video archives. 

  • Transaction layer: Own the pipeline, rights evidence, contracts, permissions, audit trail and delivery API.

  • ML and data quality: Build anonymisation across text, tables, images and video, plus re-identification checks, deduplication, quality scoring and tooling that turns raw records into training-ready data. 

  • Delivery and compute: Decide whether data is processed in our cloud or inside the supplier’s environment. Build secure delivery, recurring updates and our GPU infrastructure.

  • Technical direction: Own the architecture and roadmap. Work directly with labs, suppliers and researchers to understand what the system needs to become.

What you need to succeed

  • Data infrastructure at scale: You have built pipelines for large unstructured datasets, such as video, images, sensor logs or documents, at terabyte scale or more.

  • Physical-world data: You have worked with documents, logs, video or sensor streams, ideally in robotics, industrial or autonomous systems and know what embodied AI teams need from data and where it breaks.

  • Sensitive data: You know how to handle personal and confidential data safely. Experience with regulated data is a plus.

  • Technical leadership: You make architectural decisions, explain them clearly and raise the engineering bar as the team grows.

  • Hands-on Builder: You have taken a product, platform or open-source project from 0 to 1 that others relied on, and you still write code and own the critical paths.

  • Founder mindset: You care about the outcome, not the title. You form strong views, test them quickly and are comfortable owning technical, product and operational problems.

  • Location: Paris preferred. English required; French is a plus.
